src: The crowd cheered and drank in unison.
trg: Bato basepelaka mpe bamelaki elongo.

src: The wake went on for hours, and by the end of the night, everyone was exhausted but happy.
trg: Matanga esalaki bangonga ebele, mpe pene ya nsuka ya butu, bato nyonso balembaki kasi bazalaki na esengo.

src: But in 1974, a military junta known as the Derg seized power and began a brutal campaign of repression.
trg: Kasi na 1974, etuluku ya basoda eyebana na nkombo Derg ebotalaki bokonzi mpe ebandaka mosala ya mobulu ya konyokola bato.

src: The Derg's policies led to widespread famine and poverty, and millions of Ethiopians were forced to flee their homes.
trg: Mayele ya Derg ememaki na nzala mpe bobola ya makasi, mpe epusaki bamilio ya bato ya Ethiope na kokima bandako na bango.

src: In 1991, a coalition of rebel groups known as the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) overthrew the Derg.
trg: Na 1991, lisangani ya bituluku ya batomboki ebengami Lisanga ya Botomboki ya Demokrasi ya Bato ya Ethiopie (EPRDF) ekweisaki Derg.

src: The EPRDF established a new government and promised to restore peace and prosperity to Ethiopia.
trg: EPRDF etyaki boyangeli ya sika mpe elakaki kozongisa kimya mpe bozwi na Ethiopie.

src: However, the EPRDF's rule has been plagued by human rights abuses, corruption, and political repression.
trg: Atako bongo, boyangeli ya EPRDF ebebisamaki na kozanga kotosa balotomo ya bato, avoka, mpe kokanga bato politiki nzela ya kosala.

src: In 2018, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed took office and pledged to reform the country.
trg: Na 2018, Ministre ya Yambo Abiy Ahmed azwaki bokonzi mpe alakaki na kosala mbongwana na ekolo.

src: He released political prisoners, lifted restrictions on the media, and began peace talks with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the former ruling party of Tigray.
trg: Abimisaki bato ya politiki oyo bazalaki na boloko, alongolaki bipekiseli batyelaki bipanzi-nsango, mpe abandaki masolo ya kimya na Lisanga ya Bobikisi Bato ya Tigré (TPLF), parti ya kala oyo ezalaki koyangea Tigré.

src: However, the peace talks broke down in June 2020, and the TPLF launched an offensive against the Ethiopian military.
trg: Kasi, masolo ya kimya ekatanaki na sanza ya Motoba 2020, mpe TPLF abandaki kobundisa basoda ya Ethiopie.

src: The ensuing conflict has been devastating.
trg: Bitumba oyo ebimaki nsima ebebisa makasi mpenza.

src: The fighting has displaced millions of people, and the humanitarian situation is dire.
trg: Bitumba epusa bamilio ya bato na kokima, mpe bomoi ya bato ezali na mpasi mpenza.

src: Movies have long been a powerful force in shaping our culture and our values.
trg: Bafilme ezalaki biloko ezala na nguya makasi ya kobongisa culture mpe bizaleli na biso.

src: They can influence our beliefs about everything from love and romance to war and violence.
trg: Ekoki kozala na bopusi na bindimeli na makambo nyonso banda na boling mpe lolango kino na bitumba mpe mobulu.

src: And they have a particularly strong influence on our ideas about gender roles.
trg: Mpe ekoki kozala na bopusi ya makasi mpenza na ndenge totalelaka basi na mibali.

src: For decades, Hollywood has perpetuated the stereotype of the ideal wife as a beautiful, submissive, and domestic woman who puts her husband and children first.
trg: Banda mibu ebele, Hollywood ebanda komonisa ndakisa ya mwasi ya kokoka lokola mwasi ya kitoko, ya botosi, mpe afandaka na ndako oyo atyaka mobali na bana na ye na esika ya liboso.

src: This image is often reinforced by the way that female characters are portrayed in movies.
trg: Balendisaka likanisi wana mbala mingi na ndenge balakisaka basi na bafilme.

src: For example, a study by the Geena Davis Institute found that in the top 100 films of 2017, only 30% of female characters had speaking roles, and only 12% of those characters were working outside the home.
trg: Na ndakisa, boyekoli moko ya Geena Davis Institute emonaki ete na bafilme 100 ya liboso ya 2017, kaka 30% mpamba ya basi bazalaki na mokumba ya koloba, mpe 12% ya bato yango bazalaki kosala na libanda ya ndako.

src: The majority of female characters were portrayed as either romantic interests or mothers.
trg: Balakisaka basi ebele lokola bato bazali koluka bolingo to bamama.

src: This narrow representation of women in film sends a powerful message to viewers about what it means to be a woman.
trg: Lolenge mabe oyo bafilme emonisaka basi etindaka nsango ya makasi na batali na oyo etali kozala mwasi.

src: It suggests that women's primary role is to be attractive and nurturing, and that their success is measured by their relationships with men and children.
trg: Ezali kolakisa ete mokumba ya libosoliboso ya mwasi ezali ya kobenda mobali mpe ya koleisa, mpe batalaka kolonga na bango na boyokani na bango na mibali mpe bana.

src: This idealized image of the wife can be harmful to women in several ways.
trg: Likanisi oyo ya mwasi ekoki kozala mabe mpo na basi na balolenge ebele.

trg: Ekoki kouta na biloko ebele, neti kolya biloko batye epice ebele to ezali na mafuta mingi, komela masanga, to komela bankisi moko boye.

src: Judaism and Kosher Kosher is a set of dietary laws in Judaism.
trg: Lingomba ya Bayuda mpe Kosher Kosher ezali mibeko etali bilei na Lingomba ya Bayuda.

src: These laws define which foods are permissible to eat and which are not.
trg: Mibeko oyo elimbolaka bilei nini bakoki kolya mpe bilei nini bakoki kolya te.

src: Kosher foods are those that are considered to be fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
trg: Bilei ya Kosher ezali bilei oyo bamonaki ete ekoki kolyama na kotalela mobeko ya Bayuda.

src: The laws of kosher are based on the Torah, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.
trg: Mibeko ya kosher esimbami na Torah, babuku mitano ya liboso ya Biblia ya Kiebreo.

src: These laws prohibit the consumption of certain animals, such as pigs and shellfish, as well as the consumption of blood and meat from animals that have not been slaughtered in a specific way.
trg: Mibeko oyo epekisaka kolya banyama mosusu, neti bangulu mpe mbisi ya molungé, mpe kolya makila na misuni ya banyama oyo baboma te na ndenge moko ya sikisiki.

src: Kosher foods are also subject to a number of other regulations, such as the separation of dairy and meat products.
trg: Bilei ya kosher ezali mpe na mibeko mosusu ebele, neti kokabola biloko ya miliki mpe misuni.

src: Kosher food is prepared in a way that ensures that it is fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
trg: Bilei ya kosher elambamaka na kolanda ndenge oyo ekoki kolyama na koyokana na mobeko ya Bayuda.

src: The observance of kosher laws is an important part of Jewish religious practice.
trg: Kotosa mibeko ya kosher ezali eteni ya ntina ya mimeseno ya lingomba ya Bayuda.

src: For many Jews, eating kosher food is a way to show their devotion to God and to connect with their heritage.
trg: Mpo na Bayuda ebele, kolya bilei ya kosher ezali lolenge ya komonisa komipesa na bango na Nzambe mpe kosangisa bango na libula na bango.

src: There are a number of reasons why Jews observe kosher laws.

src: Indira Gandhi was the first and only woman to serve as Prime Minister of India.
trg: Indira Gandhi azalaki mwasi ya liboso mpe moko mpamba oyo azalaki Ministre ya Yambo na Inde.

src: She was born in 1917 into a prominent political family, and her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Prime Minister of India.
trg: Abotamaki na 1917 na libota moko ya politiki oyo eyebana, mpe papa na ye, Jawaharlal Nehru, azalaki Ministre ya Yambo ya liboso ya Inde.

src: Indira Gandhi was educated in India and England, and she married Feroze Gandhi in 1942.
trg: Indira Gandhi atangaki na Inde mpe na Angleterre, mpe abalaki Feroze Gandhi na 1942.

src: They had two sons, Rajiv and Sanjay.
trg: Bazalaki na bana-mibali mibale, Rajiv na Sanjay.

src: Gandhi began her political career in 1955, when she was elected to the Indian Parliament.
trg: Gandhi abandaki mosala ya politiki na 1955, ntango bavotaki ye na Parlema ya Inde.

src: She served in various ministerial positions in the government of her father, and in 1966 she became Prime Minister after his death.
trg: Azalaki na ministre na bisika ebele na guvernema ya papa na ye, mpe na 1966 akomaki Ministre ya Yambo nsima ya liwa ya papa na ye.

src: Gandhi was a controversial figure, and her policies were often criticized.
trg: Gandhi azalaki moto oyo bazalaki kondima te, mpe mbala mingi bato bazalaki koloba mabe mpo na mibeko na ye.

src: She was accused of being authoritarian and of suppressing dissent.
trg: Bafundaki ye ete azalaki moto ya nkanza mpe kolongola batomboki.

src: However, she was also a popular leader, and she is credited with modernizing India and improving the lives of its people.
trg: Kasi, azalaki mpe mokambi oyo bato balingaki mingi, mpe balobaki ete ye nde akomisa Inde ya sika mpe abongisa bomoi ya bato na yango.

src: Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.
trg: Babomaki Gandhi na basoda babatelaka ye Sikh na 1984.

src: She was succeeded by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.
trg: Mwana na ye ya mobali Rajiv Gandhi, azwaki esika na ye.

src: Gandhi's life and career were marked by many challenges, but she never gave up on her dream of a better India.
trg: Bomoi mpe mosala ya Ghandi ezalaki na mikakatano ebele, kasi atikala kosundola te ndoto na ye ya kozala na Inde ya malamu.

trg: Nsukansuka, ekomaki ngala na nga, mpe nalakisaki bafoto na nga na wapi oyo azalaki na comptoire.

src: She looked at it for a moment, then shook her head.
trg: Atalaki yango mwa moke, na nsima aningisaki moto.

src: "I'm sorry," she said. "We can't accept this portfolio. It's not up to our standards."

src: I felt a wave of despair wash over me.
trg: Nayokaki kozanga elikya ezwi nga.

src: All my hard work, for nothing.
trg: Mosala na nga nyonso ya makasi, ekei mpamba.

src: I took the portfolio back and started to walk away.
trg: Nazwaki bafoto na nga mpe nabandaki kokende.

src: "Wait," the woman called "I can see that you've put a lot of effort into this. Why don't you take a seat over there and I'll see what I can do."
trg: "Zela," ana ndenge mwasi yango alobaki "Namoni ete osalaki milende mingi mpo na yango. Soki olingi okoki kofanda kuna mpe nakotala nini nakoki kosala."

src: I sat down and waited.
trg: Nafandaki mpe nazelaki.

src: A few minutes later, the woman came back.
trg: Miniki moke na nsima, mwasi wana azongaki.

src: "I've talked to my manager," she said.
trg: "Nasololi na mokonzi na nga," wana maloba na ye.

src: "We're willing to make an exception for you. We'll accept your portfolio, but you'll have to pay a processing fee."
trg: "Tolingi kosala exception mpo na yo. Tokondima bafoto na yo, kasi osengeli kofuta mwa mosola ya misala."

src: I sighed.
trg: Nakitisaki motema.

src: It was a lot of money, but I didn't have any other choice.
trg: Ezalaki mbongo ebele, kasi nazalaki te na eloko mosusu ya kosala.

src: In the 2006 teen comedy She's the Man, Amanda Bynes plays Viola Hastings, a high school student who disguises herself as a boy in order to play on the boys' soccer team.
trg: Na filme ya kosekisa ya bilenge ya 2006 Azali Mobali, Amanda Bynes assali role ya Viola Hastings, moyekoli ya secondaire oyo amimonisi lokola mwana-mobali mpo na kobeta na ekipe ya ndembo ya bana-mibali.

src: The film is full of laugh-out-loud moments, thanks to Bynes's spot-on comedic timing and delivery.
trg: Filme etondi na bantango ya koseka makasi, na lisalisi ya kosekisa ya malamu mpe ebongi ya Bynes.

src: She is able to perfectly capture the awkwardness and uncertainty of a teenage boy, while still maintaining her own unique brand of humor.
trg: Azali na makoki ya komonisa malamu mpenza bozoba mpe kozanga makoki ya elenge mobali, ksi azali kobatela mpe mayele na ye moko ya kosekisa.

src: The supporting cast is also excellent, with Channing Tatum, Laura Ramsey, and Vinnie Jones all giving memorable performances.
trg: Basungi basali mpe mosala ya kitoko, na Channing Tatum, Laura Ramsey, mpe Vinnie Jones bango nyonso basali mosala ya kokamwisa.

src: The film's director, Andy Fickman, does a great job of balancing the humor with the drama, creating a film that is both funny and heartwarming.
trg: Mokambi ya filme, Andy Fickman, asali mosala ya makasi ya kosangisa kosekisa na drame, asali filme oyo ezali kosekisa mpe kosimba motema.

src: She's the Man is a classic teen comedy that is sure to please fans of the genre.
trg: Azali Mobali ezali filme ya kosekisa ya kitoko mpo na bilenge oyo ekozanga to kosepelisa bango.

src: Bynes's performance is a standout, and the film is full of laugh-out-loud moments.
trg: Byne asali mosala ya malamu mpenza, mpe filme wana etondi na bantango ya koseka makasi.

src: If you're looking for a fun and entertaining movie to watch, I highly recommend checking out She's the Man.
trg: Soki ozali koluka filme ye kosekisa mpe ya kitoko ya kotala, nalendisi yo makasi na koluka Azali Mobali.

src: In addition to being a great comedy, She's the Man is also a film with a strong message about gender equality.
trg: Longola kozala filme ya kosekisa ya kitoko, Azali Mobali ezali mpe filme oyo ezali na nsango ya makasi mpo na bokokani kati ya basi na mibali.

src: Viola's decision to disguise herself as a boy in order to play on the boys' soccer team is a powerful statement about the importance of breaking down gender stereotypes.
trg: Ekateli ya Viola ya komimonisa lokola mwana-mobali mpo na kobeta ndembo na ekipe ya mibali ezali liloba makasi mpo na ntina ya kolongola makanisi oyo bato bazalaka na yango mpo na basi na mibali.

src: The film shows that girls can be just as good as boys at sports, and that they should not be held back by their gender.
trg: Filme ezali kolakisa ete bana-basi bakoki kozala makasi na masano lokola bana-mibale, mpe ete kibomwasi na bango esengeli kozongisa bango te nsima.

src: She's the Man is a film that is both funny and inspiring.
trg: Azali Mobali na filme moko oyo ezali kosekisa mpe kopesa makanisi.

src: It is a great choice for anyone who is looking for a feel-good movie with a message.
trg: Ezali liponi ya malamu mpo na moto nyonso oyo azali koluka filme ya malamu ezali na mesage.

src: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity, one of the two pillars of modern physics (alongside quantum mechanics).
trg: Albert Einstein abotamaki na Allemagne, azalaki moto ya physique ya théroie oyo abimisaki liteya ya rélativité, moko ya makonzi mibale ya physique ya lelo (elongo na mecanique quantum).

src: His work is also known for its influence on the philosophy of science.
trg: Mosala na ye eyebana mpe mpo na bopusi na yo na filozofi ya siansi.

src: Einstein is best known in popular culture for his mass–energy equivalence formula E = mc2 (which has been dubbed "the world's most famous equation").
trg: Einstein ayebana mingi na culture ya bato nyonso mpo na bokokanisi na ye ya formule masse=energie E = mc2 (oyo babengaka "equation eyebana mingi na mokili").

src: Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, German Empire, on 14 March 1879.
trg: Einstein abotamaki na Ulm, na Bokonzi ya Württemberg, Bokonzi ya Allemagne, na 14 sanza ya Misato 1879.

src: He showed an early aptitude for mathematics and physics.
trg: Alakisaki na ebandeli ete azalaki na mayele ya matematike mpe physique.

src: In 1905, at the age of 26, Einstein published four groundbreaking papers that transformed physics.
trg: Na 1905, na mbula 26, Einstein bapapier minei ya sika mpenza oyo ebongolaki physique.

src: These include his special relativity theory, which introduced the concepts of space and time as a single unified continuum, and his general relativity theory, which proposed that gravity is not a force, but is instead a curvature of spacetime.
trg: Yango etali liteya ya speciale ya relativité, oyo ekotisaka makanisi ya espace mpe ntango lokola eloko oyo elandanaka, mpe liteya na ya generale ya relavité, oyo elobaki ete gravité ezali te nguya, kasi courbure ya eleko ya ntango.

src: Einstein's work led to a new understanding of the universe, and had a profound impact on the development of modern physics.
trg: Mosala ya Einstein ememakki na koyeba universe ndenge mosusu, mpe ezala na bopusi makasi na bokoli ya physique ya lelo.

src: He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his explanation of the photoelectric effect.
trg: Azwaki Mbano ya Nobel ya Physique na 1921 mpo na ndimbola na ye effect photoelectrique.

src: Einstein was a pacifist and a strong advocate for social justice.
trg: Einstein azalaki motyei kimya mpe moto azalaki kokotela mingi boyengebene mpo na bato nyonso.

src: Many people wake up before sunrise to start their day's work.
trg: Bato ebele batelemi liboso moi ebima mpo na kobanda mosala na bango ya mokolo.

src: Farmers may rise before dawn to milk their cows or tend to their crops.
trg: Basali-bilanga bakoki kolamuka liboso ntongo etana mpo na kobimisa miliki na bangombe na bango to kobongisa milona bango.

src: Fishermen may go out to sea before the sun comes up.
trg: Balobi-mbisi bakoki kokende na mbu liboso moi ebima.

src: People who work in the city may also wake up early to catch the bus or train to work.
trg: Bato oyo basalaka na engumba bakoki kotelema na ntongo makasi mpo na kozwa bisi to engunduka mpo na mosala.

src: Once people are up, they typically eat a simple breakfast of porridge, bread, or tea.
trg: Soki bato batelemi, mbala mingi balyaka potopto, mampa, to thé.

src: Then they get ready for the day.
trg: Na nsima bazalaka ya kobongama mpo na mokolo.

src: Many people in The Gambia wear traditional clothing, such as long dresses or skirts for women and long pants or shirts for men.
trg: Bato ebele na Gambie balataka bilamba ya mboka, neti barobe to bajupe ya milai mpo na basi mpe bapantalo to bajupe ya milai mpo na mibali.

src: They may also wear a headscarf or cap.
trg: Bakoki mpe kolata elamba ya moto to ekoti.

src: After breakfast, people go about their daily activities.
trg: Nsima ya kolya ya ntongo, bato bakendaka na misala na bango ya mokolo na mokolo.

src: Children go to school, while adults go to work.
trg: Bana bakendaka na kelasi, kasi mikolo bakendaka na mosala.

src: Many people in The Gambia work in agriculture, fishing, or tourism.
trg: Bato ebele ya Gambie basalaka mosala ya bilanga, ya koloba, to ya toursime.

src: Others work in government, business, or education.
trg: Basusu basalaka na guvernema, na mumbongo, to na biteyelo.

src: In the afternoon, people may take a break from work to relax or socialize.
trg: Na nsima ya midi, bato bakoki kopema na mosala mpo na kominanola to kokutana na bato mosusu.

src: They may go for a walk, visit friends and family, or play games.
trg: Bakoki kokende kotambola, kokende kotala baninga mpe libota, to kobeta masano.

src: In the evening, people often eat dinner with their families.
trg: Na butu, mbala mingi bato balyaka na mabota na bango.

src: Dinner is typically a simple meal of rice, vegetables, and meat or fish.
trg: Mbala mingi bilei ya mpokwa ezalaka ya bilei ya pete neti loso, banduda, mpe misuni to mbisi.

src: A seed is a small, dormant plant embryo that is capable of developing into a new plant under the right conditions.
trg: Molona ezali mwa nzete moko oyo ekoki kokola mpe kokoma nzete ya sika soki ezali na esika ya malamu.

src: When a seed sprouts, it begins to grow roots and shoots.
trg: Soki molona ebimi, ebandaka kobimisa misisa mpe mwa mito.

src: The roots anchor the plant in the soil and absorb water and nutrients from the ground.
trg: Misisa ekandaka nzete na mabele mpe ezwaka mai mpe bilei na mabele.

src: The shoots grow upwards towards the sun, and the leaves begin to photosynthesize, producing food for the plant.
trg: Mito ya mike ebimaki na ngambo ya moi, mpe matiti ebandaka photosynthese, ebimisaka bilei mpo na nzete.

src: As the plant grows, it develops a stem, leaves, flowers, and fruit.
trg: Ntango nzete ezali kokola, ebimisaka tige, matiti, bafololo mpe bambuma.

src: The flowers produce seeds, which are dispersed by wind, water, or animals.
trg: Bafololo ebotaka bambuma, oyo mopepe, mai to banyama epanzaka.

src: When a seed lands in a suitable location, it can germinate and begin the process of growth all over again.
trg: Soki molona ekwei na esika ya malamu, ekoki kobota mpe kobanda na kokola mpenza.

src: The process of seed germination is a marvel of nature.
trg: Kokola ya molona ezali likamwisi ya bozalisi.

src: It is a testament to the power of life and the resilience of the natural world.
trg: Emonisaka nguya ya bomoi mpe molende ya bozalisi.

src: When a seed sprouts, it is a sign of hope and new beginnings.
trg: Soki molona ebimi, ezali elembo ya elikya mpe ebandeli ya sika.

src: Grace: Can you tell me a little bit about its history?
trg: Grace: Okoki kobetela nga mwa mokie lisolo wana?

src: Teacher: Of course. Tea originated in China, where it has been cultivated for over 5,000 years.
trg: Molakisi: Ya solo. Thé eutaki na Chine, esika babandaki kolona yango banda mibu koleka 5 000.

src: The first written record of tea dates back to the 3rd century BC, when it was mentioned in a Chinese medical text.
trg: Makambo ya liboso bakomaki mpo na thé ebandaka na ekeke ye 3 BC, ntango balobelaki yango na mikanda ya kimonganga ya Chine.

src: Tea was originally used as a medicinal herb, but it quickly became a popular drink among Chinese people of all social classes.
trg: Na ebandeli bazalaki kosalela thé lokola nkisi ya matiti, kasi nokinoki bato nyonso ya Chine bakomaki kolinga komela yango.

src: Grace: What about outside of China? When did tea start to spread to other parts of the world?
trg: Grace: Ebongo libanda ya Chine? Ntango nini thé ebandaki kopanzana na biteni mosusu ya mokili?

src: Teacher: Tea was first introduced to Europe in the 16th century by Portuguese traders.
trg: Molakisi: Bamemaki thé na Eropa na ekeke ya 16 na bateki ya Portugal.

src: It quickly became popular among European elites, and by the 18th century, tea had become a staple of British culture.
trg: Ekomaki noki kolingama mingi na bakonzi ya Eropa, mpe na ekeke ya 18, thé ekomaki eloko ya ntina ya cultue ya Grande-Bretagne.

src: In the 19th century, tea was also introduced to North America, where it became a popular drink among both colonists and Native Americans.
trg: Na ekeke ya 19, bakotisaki thé na Amerika ya Norde, esika bacolon na Bana-Mboka ya Amerika bakomaki kolongi komela yango mingi.

src: Grace: That's really interesting.I never knew that tea had such a long history.
trg: Grace: Ezali kobenda mpenza likebi. Nayeba nanu te ete thé ezali na lisolo ya molai boye.

src: Teacher: It's a fascinating story, and it's one that's still being written today.
trg: Molakisi: Ezali lisolo ya kitoko, mpe ezali lisolo bazali kokoba kokoma lelo.

src: I know what you did yesterday.
trg: Nayebi makambo osalaki lobi.

src: You posted a picture of yourself wearing that green rag on social media.
trg: Otyaki bafoto na yo olati eloko wana ya vert na reseaux sociaux.

src: I know you thought it was funny, but it wasn’t.
trg: Nayebi okanisaki ezali kosekisa, kasi ezalaki bongo te.

src: It was disrespectful to your mother, and it hurt her feelings.
trg: Ezalaki kofingisa mama na yo, mpe ezokisaki mayoki na ye.

src: I’m not asking you to apologize because I’m mad at you.
trg: Nazali kosenga yo te na kosenga bolimbisi mpo nasilikeli yo.

src: I’m asking you to apologize because it’s the right thing to do.
trg: Nazali kosenga na kosenga bolimbisi mpo ezali likambo ya malamu ya kosala.

src: Your mother loves you, and she deserves your respect.
trg: Mama alingaka yo, mpe esengeli otosa ye.

src: Please call her today and tell her you’re sorry.
trg: Palado benga ye lelo mpe senga ye bolimbisi.

src: Tell her that you didn’t mean to hurt her feelings, and that you promise to never wear that green rag again.
trg: Yebisa ye ete olingaki te kozokisa mayoki na ye, mpe ete olaki ete okotikala lisusu te kolata eloko wana ya vert.

src: I know you’re a good person, and I know you love your mother.
trg: Nayebi ozali moto malamu, mpe nayebi olingaka mama na yo.

src: So please, do the right thing and apologize.
trg: Palado, salaka eloko ya malamu mpe senga bolimbisi.

src: After you apologize to your mother, I want you to burn that green rag.
trg: Nsima ya kosenga mama bolimbisi, nalingi ozikisa eloko wana ya vert.

src: It’s a symbol of your disrespect, and it needs to be gone.
trg: Ezali elembo ya kozanga botosi na yo, mpe esengeli kolimwa.

src: I know it might be hard to let go of that rag, but it’s important.
trg: Nayebi ekoki kozala mpasi na kobwaka eloko wana, kasi ezali ntina.

src: It’s a symbol of your past, and it’s time to move on.
trg: Ezali elembo ya mikolo na yo eleki, mpe ezali ntango ya kokende liboso.

src: You’re a new person now.
trg: Ozali moto ya sika sikoyo.

src: You’re a better person.
trg: Ozali moto ya malamu.

src: And you don’t need that rag to define you anymore.
trg: Mpe olingi te ete eloko elimbola yo lisusu.

src: So please, burn it.
trg: Palado, zikisa yango.

src: Burn it and let it go.
trg: Zikisa yango mpe tika ekende.

src: And then go hug your mother and tell her you love her.
trg: Mpe na nsima kende koyamba mama na yo mpe yebisa ye olingaka ye.

src: She loves you too.
trg: Alingaka yo mpe.

src: A car was driving too fast and lost control, swerving into the other lane and hitting a car head-on.
trg: Motuka moko ezalaki kotambola noki mpenza mpe bazalaki kokamba yango lisusu te, ekendaki na nzela mosus mpe etutaka motuka moko na liboso.

src: The driver of the first car was killed instantly, and the driver of the second car was seriously injured.
trg: Mokumbi ya motuka ya liboso akufaki na mbala moko, mpe mokumbi ya motuka ya mibale azokaki makasi.

src: My friend Joseph called me to talk about it.
trg: Moninga na nga Joseph abengaki nga mpo tolobela yango.

src: "It's so sad," he said. "I can't imagine how the families of the victims are coping."
trg: "Ezali mawa," wana maloba na ye. "Nazali koyeba te ndenge mabota ya bato bafuki bazali kobunda."

src: "Me neither," I responded. "It's a reminder that we need to be careful when we're driving.
trg: "Nga mpe nayebi te," wana eyano na nga. "Ezali kokundwela biso ete tosengeli kokeba ntango tozali kokumba.

src: Even a small mistake can have devastating consequences."
trg: Ata libunga ya moke ekoki kozala na baconsequence ya mabe mpenza."

src: "I agree," replied Jo. "We all need to follow the rules of the road and drive defensively."
trg: "Nandimi," wana eyano ya Jo. "Bison yonso tosengeli kotosa mibeko ya nzela mpe kokumba na ndenge ebongi."

src: "Absolutely," I quickly added. "And we need to be aware of the dangers of distracted driving. Things like texting and talking on the phone can take our attention away from the road and lead to accidents."
trg: "Ezali solo," nandimaki mbala moko. "Mpe tosengeli koyeba makama kokumba kozanga likebi. Makambo neti kokoma mesage to kosola na telfone ekoki kolongola likebi na biso na nzela mpe komema ba aksida."

src: "I know," said Jo sheepishly. "I'm guilty of it myself sometimes."
trg: "Nayebi," Jo ayanola na nsoni. "Nga moko nasala mabunga wana ntango mosusu."

src: In the small town of Malgudi, there was a corrupt police inspector named Ramasamy.
trg: Na mboka moke ya Malfudi, ezali na mokonzi ya polisi moko oyo azwaka avoka nkombo na ye Ramasamy.

src: He would often take bribes from the people he arrested, and he would also use his power to harass and intimidate people.
trg: Azalaki kozwa mbala mingi avoka na bato azalaki kokanga, mpe azalaki kosalela bokonzi na ye mpo na konyokola mpe kobangisa bato.

src: One day, Ramasamy arrested a young man named Krishnan for a crime he did not commit.
trg: Mokolo moko, Ramasamy akangaki elenge mobali moko nkombo na ye Krishnan mpo na mbeba oyo asalaki te.

src: Krishnan was innocent, but Ramasamy refused to listen to him.
trg: Krishnana ayebaki eloko te, kasi Ramasamy aboyaki koyokela ye.

src: He demanded a bribe from Krishnan, and when Krishnan refused to pay, Ramasamy threw him in jail.
trg: Asengaki Krishnana mbongo, mpe ntango Krishnan aboyaki kofura, Ramasamy atyaki ye na boloko.

src: Krishnan's father, a poor farmer, was desperate to get his son out of jail.
trg: Papa ya Krishnan, mobola oyo asalaka bilanga, ezalaki na mposa ya kobimisa mwana na ye na boloko.

src: He went to see Ramasamy and begged him to release Krishnan, but Ramasamy refused.
trg: Akendaki komona Ramasamy mpe abondelaki ye abimisa Krishnan, kasi Ramasamy aboyaki.

src: The farmer then went to the local temple and prayed to God for help.
trg: Na nsima mosali-bilanga akendaki na tempelo ya mboka mpe abondelaki Nzambi mpo asalisaka ye.

src: The next day, the farmer was walking home from the temple when he saw a large snake crossing the road.
trg: Mokolo elandaka, mosali-bilanga azalaki kozonga na ndako nsima ya kouta na tempelo mpe amonaki nyoka monana ezali kokatisa nzela.

src: The farmer was afraid of snakes, but he knew that he had to do something to help his son.
trg: Mosali-bilanga azalaki kobanga banyoka, kasi ayebaki ete asengeli kosala eloko mpo na kosalisa mwana na ye.

src: He picked up the snake and carried it to the police station.
trg: Akamataki nyoka wana mpe amemaki yango na biro ya bapolisi.

src: When Ramasamy saw the snake, he was terrified.
trg: Ntango Ramasamy amonaki nyoka, abangaki makasi.

src: Dear [Name], I hope this letter finds you well.
trg: Ndeko [Nkombo], Nakanisi mokanda oyo ekuti yo ozali malamu.

src: I'm writing to you from our family farm, where the harvest has been going well this year.
trg: Nazali kokomela yo uta na ferme na biso ya libota, esika mosala ya kolongola biloko na bilanga ezali kosalema malamu mbula oyo.

src: We're expecting a bumper crop of sugarcane, which is used to make rum.
trg: Tozali kozela kolongola bakoko ebele, oyo basalelaka mpo na kosala rhum.

src: Rum is a distilled spirit made from sugarcane molasses or sugarcane juice.
trg: Ezali masanga basalaka na banzete ya koko to na mai ya koko.

src: It's typically aged in wooden barrels, which gives it its characteristic flavor.
trg: Eumelaka na milangi ya mabaya, yango epesaka yango kitoko na yango oyo eyebana.

src: Rum can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or mixed in cocktails.
trg: Okoki komela rhum yango moko, na baglase, to ya kosangisa na cocktails.

src: There are many different types of rum, each with its own unique flavor profile.
trg: Ezali na balolenge mingi ekeseni ya rhum, mokomoko ezalaki na elengi na yango ekeseni.

src: Some of the most popular types of rum include light rum, dark rum, and spiced rum.
trg: Ndambo ya balolenge ya rhum oyo eyebana mingi ezali rhum ya makasi te, rhum ya moindo, mpe rhum ya epcié.

src: Light rum is typically made from molasses and has a light, sweet flavor.
trg: Rhum ya makasi te esalemaka na banzete mpe ezalaka na elengi ya makasi mpe sukali.

src: Dark rum is made from sugarcane juice and has a richer, more complex flavor.
trg: Rhum ya moindo esalemaka na mai ya koko mpe ezalaka na elenge ebele mpe makasi.

src: Spiced rum is made with added spices, such as cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
trg: Rhum epicé esalemaka na kobakisaka biloko neti cannelle, ndika ya muscade, mpe clous de giroffe.

src: Rum is a versatile spirit that can be used in a variety of cocktails.
trg: Rhum esali masanga oyo ekoki kosalelama na ba cocktails ya ndenge na ndenge.

src: Some classic rum cocktails include the daiquiri, the mojito, and the pina colada.
trg: Balolenge mosusu ya rhum ya cocktails oyo eyebani ezali daiquiri, mojito, mpe pina colada.

src: Rum can also be used in more creative cocktails, such as the Hemingway Daiquiri or the Painkiller.
trg: Rhum ekoki mpe kosalelama na ba cokctails ya kitoko koleka, neti Hemingway Daiquiri to Painkiller.

trg: Tosengeli koboya nguya ya bokabwani mpe ya koyina.

src: We must break the chains of poverty and ignorance.
trg: Tosengeli kokata miniololo ya bobola mpe ya kozanga koyeba.

src: And we must bind ourselves together in a common purpose: to build a better future for Nigeria.
trg: Mpe tosengeli kokangama biso nyonso elongo mpo na mokano moko: kosala avenire ya malamu mpo na Nigeria.

src: The destiny of Nigeria is not to be a land of division and conflict.
trg: Destin ya Nigeria ezali te ete ezala mokili ya kokabwana mpe ya bitumba.

src: It is to be a land of unity and progress.
trg: Esengeli ezala mboka ya bomoko mpe ezali kokola.

src: It is to be a land where everyone has a chance to succeed, regardless of their background or circumstances.
trg: Esengeli kozala mboka oyo bato nyonso baza na libaku ya kolonga, ata libota to bomoi na bango ezali ndenge nini.

src: But we cannot achieve this future without working together.
trg: Kasi tokoki te kozala na avenire wana soki tozali te kosala elongo.

src: We must reject the forces that seek to divide us and come together as one people.
trg: Tosengeli kobwaka banguya oyo elukaka kokabola biso mpe tosengeli kosangana biso nyonso elongo.

src: We must break the chains of poverty and ignorance that hold us back.
trg: Tosengeli kokata minyololo ya bobola mpe ya kozanga koyeba oyo ezongisaka biso nsima.

src: The future of Nigeria is in our hands.
trg: Avenire ya Nigeria ezali na maboko na biso moko.

src: Let us not squander it.
trg: Tobebisa yango te.

src: Let us reject, break and bind the forces that seek to control and pervert our destiny.
trg: Totika, tokata mpe tokanga banguya oyo elukaka koyangela mpe kobebisa destin na biso.

src: Let us come together as one people and build a better future for all.

src: "Complete your Amazon shopping experience with our new and improved ad service!" the ad read.
trg: "Silisa eksperianse na yo ya kosomba na Amazon na mosala na biso ya sika mpe oyo babongisi!" wana maloba ya piblisite.

src: "With our service, you'll never have to worry about missing out on a great deal again.
trg: "Na misala na biso, okomitungisa te ete ozangi lisusu eloko moko ya ntina.

src: Just sit back and relax, and we'll take care of the rest.
trg: Vanda kaka na nsima mpe minyolisa, mpe tosala nyonso oyo etikali.

src: Our service is completely free to use, and it's easy to get started.
trg: Mosala na biso ezalaka mpenza ya ofele na kosalela, mpe ezali pete na kobanda.

src: Just sign up for an account and start adding products to your cart.
trg: Komisa nkombo mpo na kofungola konti mpe banda kobakisa biloko na pusu na yo.

src: When you're ready to check out, our service will automatically find the best deals for you and apply them to your order.
trg: Soki kobongami mpo totalela yango, mosala na biso ekozwa na mbala moko biloko ebongi mpenza mpo na yo mpe kosalela yango na komande na yo.

src: So what are you waiting for?
trg: Ebongo ozali kozela nini?

src: Sign up for our service today and start saving money on all your Amazon purchases!"
trg: Komisa nkombo na mosala na biso lelo mpe banda kobomba mosola na bosombi nyonso ya Amazon!"

src: As the customer clicked on the ad, they were whisked away to a new website.
trg: Soki kiliya afini the piblisite, bamemamaki na site internet ya sika.

src: The website was full of ads for all sorts of products, all of which were supposedly on sale.
trg: Site internet wana etondaki na bapiblisite mpo na biloko ya nyonso, oyo ndenge balobaki ezalaki ya koteka.

src: The customer was tempted to buy a few things, but they hesitated.
trg: Kiliya abendamaki na kosomba mwa biloko, kasi azalaki na badute.

src: They had heard stories about people getting scammed by online ads, and they didn't want to be one of them.
trg: Ayokaki masolo ya batu oyo bakosaki bango na bapiblisite na internet, mpe alingaki te kozala moko na bango.

src: The customer decided to do some research on the company that was running the ad.
trg: Kiliya azwaki ekateli ya kosala mwa bolukiluki na kompani oyo ezalaki kosala piblisite wana.

src: They found a few negative reviews, but most of the reviews were positive.
trg: Amonaki mwa bakomantere ya mabe mpo na bango, kasi bakomantere mingi ezalaki ya malamu.

src: "So, I was just on the internet, minding my own business, when I saw this pop-up ad that said I had a virus on my computer.
trg: "Yango wana, nazalaki kaka na internet, nazali kokanisa mosala na nga moko, ntango namonaki piblisite oyo ebimi, elobi nazali na virisi na ordinatere na nga.

src: I was like, "What? No way!"
trg: Nazali neti, "Nini? Ekoki kosalema te!"

src: But then I clicked on it, and it took me to this website that looked really official, and it said that I needed to download this software to fix the virus.
trg: Kasi na nsima nafinaki yango, mpe ememaki nga na site internet wana oyoi ezalaki komonana ya solo mpenza, mpe elobaki ete nasengeli kozwa logiciel oyo mpo na kolongola virisi.

src: So I did, and I installed it, and then it started filling my computer with all this malware.
trg: Nasalaki yango, mpe na instalaki yango, mpe na nsima ebandaki kotondisa ordinatere na nga na ba logiciel nyonso oyo ya mabe.

src: I was so mad!
trg: Epesaki nga nkanda!

src: I tried to uninstall it, but it wouldn't let me.
trg: Namekaki kolongola yango, kasi ezalaki kondima te.

src: I finally had to take my computer to a repair shop, and they had to wipe the whole thing and reinstall Windows.
trg: Nsukansuka namekaki ordinatere na nga na butiki mpo babongisa yango, mpe esengaki balongola biloko nyonso mpe ba install Windows.

src: It was a total nightmare.
trg: Ezalaki likambo ya mabe mpenza.

src: So, that's why I'm always so careful about clicking on pop-up ads.
trg: Yango wana, nazalaka ntango nyonso mayele liboso ya kofina biplisite oyo ebimi.

src: You never know what they're going to do.
trg: Oyebi ata moke te nini bakosala.

src: They could be filled with malware, or they could steal your personal information.
trg: Bakoki kotondisa yo na ba logiciel ya mabe, to bakoki koyiba bansango na yo.

src: It's just not worth the risk.
trg: Esengeli komitya na likama.

src: If you ever see a pop-up ad that looks suspicious, just close it and don't click on it.
trg: Soki omoni piblisite ebimi oyo ezali komonana neti ya mabe, kanga kaka mpe kofina te.

src: And if you're ever not sure whether or not it's safe, just don't do it.
trg: Mpe soki oyebi te soki ezali malamu to te, kosala yango te.

src: Here is a delicious pork dish from the county of Lancashire.
trg: Oyo elubu ya kitoko ya ngulu ya comté ya Lancashire.

src: Ingredients: 1kg pork belly, 1 tbsp English mustard, 1 tbsp black treacle, 1 tbsp cider vinegar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 large onion, 4 cloves garlic, 2 bay leaves, 1 sprig of thyme, 100ml cider, 100ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp cornflour, 2 tbsp cold water.
trg: Ingredients: 1kg ya ntolo ya ngulu, 1 lutu ya moke ya mustarde ya ba Anglais, 1 lutu ya moke ya melasse ya moindo, 1 lutu ya moke ya vinegre ya cidre, 1 lutu ya moke ya supu ya Worcestershire, 1 lutu ya moke ya mafuta ya bandunda, 1 litungulu ya monene, 4 ail, 2 nkasa ya laurier, 1 eteni ya thym, 100ml cidre, 100ml nsoso batokisa, 1 lutu ya moke maizena, 2 lutu ya moke mai ya malili.

src: 1. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
trg: 1. Tya moto na foure na 180 degree.

src: 2. Trim the pork belly of any excess fat and score the skin in a criss-cross pattern.
trg: 2. Longola mafuta oyo etikali na ntolo ya ngulu mpe kata mposo na yango lokola ekulusu.

src: 3. In a bowl, mix together the mustard, treacle, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and oil.
trg: 3. Na sani, sangisa yango na mustarde, melase, vinegre, supu ya Worcestershire mpe mafuta.

src: Rub this mixture all over the pork belly.
trg: Pakola biloko wana osangisi na ntolo ya ngulu.

src: 4. Place the pork belly in a roasting tin and roast in the oven for 2 hours, or until the skin is golden brown and the meat is cooked through.
trg: 4. Tya ntolo ya ngulu na kikalungu ya kotumba mpe tumba yango na foure bangonga 2, to kino mposo ekokoma wolo makasi mpe mosuni ekobela.

src: 5. While the pork is roasting, finely chop the onion, garlic, bay leaves and thyme.
trg: 5. Ntango ngulu ezali kotumbama, tuta na malembe litungulu, ail, nkasa ya laurier mpe tym.

src: Nelson Mandela is a South African anti-apartheid revolutionary, political leader, and philanthropist who served as the first black president of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.
trg: Nelson Mandela ezali motelemi ya bokabwani ya baindo na mindele na Afrika ya Sude, mokambi ya politiki, moto asalaka makambo ya malamu oyo azalaki prezida ya liboso ya moindo ya Afrika ya Sude banda 1994 kino 1999.

src: He is widely regarded as one of the most significant figures in world history.
trg: Bantu mingi bamonaka ye lokola moto ya ntina mingi na lisolo ya mokili mobimba.

src: Mandela was born in 1918 in Mvezo, South Africa.
trg: Mandela abotamaki na 1918 na Mvezo, Afrika ya Sude.

src: He grew up in a rural village and was educated at a Methodist mission school.
trg: Akolaki na mboka mpe atangaka na eteyelo ya mission ya ba Metodiste.

src: After high school, he studied law at the University of Fort Hare.
trg: Nsima ya kosilisa kelasi, atangaka mibeko na Iniveriste ya Fort Hare.

src: In 1944, he joined the African National Congress (ANC), a political organization that was fighting against apartheid.
trg: Na 1944, akotaki na Congrés National Africain (ANC), lisanga moko ya politiki oyo ezalaki kobundisa bokabwani kati ya baindo na mindele.

src: Mandela was arrested for his political activities in 1962 and sentenced to life in prison.
trg: Bakangaki Mandela mpo na misala na ye ya politiki na 1962 mpe bakatelaki ye etumbu ya boloko bomoi mobimba.

src: He spent 27 years in prison, during which time he became a symbol of the anti-apartheid movement.
trg: Alekisaka mibu 27 na boloko, na ntango wana akomaki elembo ya muvema oyo ezalaki kotelemela bokabwani kati ya baindo na mindele.

src: In 1990, Mandela was released from prison and elected president of South Africa in 1994.
trg: Na 1990, babimisaki Mandela na boloko mpe bavotaki ye prezida ya Afrika ya Sude na 1994.

src: As president, Mandela worked to unite South Africa and promote reconciliation between blacks and whites.
trg: Lokola prezida, Mandela asalaka mosala mpo na kosangisa bato ya Afrika ya Sude mpe kolendisa boyokani kati ya baindo na mindele.

src: He also oversaw the end of apartheid and the transition to a democratic government.
trg: Alandelaki mpe nsuka ya bokabwani kati na mindele na baindo mpe bokoti na guvernema ya demokrasi.

src: Mandela is a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and has been awarded numerous other honors.
trg: Mandela azwaki mbano ya Libonza ya Nobel ya Kimya mpe bapesa ye mbano ebele mosusu.

src: Using data to help people with mental health issues is a relatively new field, but it is showing great promise.
trg: Kosalela badonnée mpo na kosalisa bato bazali kobela maladi ya moto ezali liteya ya sika mpenza, kasi ezali komonisa ete ekosalia mpenza.

src: One example is the use of data to personalize therapy for patients.
trg: Ndakisa moko ezali kosalela badonnée mpo na kopesa nkisi ebongi na mobeli mokomoko.

src: By looking at a patient's individual data, therapists can better understand their needs and create a treatment plan that is tailored to them.
trg: Soki bazali kotala badonnée ya mobeli mokolo, minganga bakoki koyeba malamu mposa na ye mpe kopona bankisi ya kopesa ye oyo ebongi mpenza na ye.

src: This can lead to better outcomes for patients, as they are more likely to receive the help that they need.
trg: Ekoki kobimisa mbano malamu mpo na babeli, mpo emonani ete bakozwa mpenza lisungi oyo bazali na mposa na yango.

src: One study, which was published in the journal "JAMA Psychiatry," found that patients who received personalized therapy based on their data were more likely to improve their symptoms than those who received standard therapy.
trg: Boyekoli moko, oyo ebimisamaki na zulunalo "JAMA Psychiatry," emonaki ete babeli oyo bazwaki bankisi babongisi mpo na bango na kotalela badonnée na bango bakoki kobongisa bilembo na bango koleka baoyo bazwaki bankisi oyo bapesaka bato nyonso.

src: The study also found that the patients who received personalized therapy were more likely to stay in treatment for longer periods of time.
trg: Boyekoli yango emonaki mpe ete babeli oyo bazwaki bankisi babongisi kaka mpo na bango balingaki kokoba kozwa bankisi na bango na eleko ya molai mpenza.

src: This study is just one example of how data can be used to improve mental health care.
trg: Boyekoli oyo ezali kaka ndakisa moko ya ndenge badonnée ekoki kosalelama mpo na kobongisa bankisi ya maladi ya moto.

src: As more research is done in this area, we can expect to see even more advances in the use of data to help people with mental health issues.
trg: Bolukiluki mosusu ezali esalema na likambo oyo, tokoki kozela na komona bakoli mingi na kosalela badonnée mpo na kosalisa bato oyo bazali na maladi ya moto.

src: My sister is a therapist who uses data to help her patients.
trg: Ndeko na nga ya mwasi azali monganga oyo asalelaka badonnée mpo na kosalisa babeli.

src: The stainless steel plate is a good conductor of heat, so it can help to dissipate heat from the fire, while the fire proof rock wool is a good insulator, so it can help to prevent the fire from spreading.
trg: Plake ya acier egugaka te ememaka moto malamu, yango wana ekoki kosalisa na kolongola chaleur na moto, kasi laine ya roche oyo ezikaka te ezali isolant ya malamu, yango wana ekoki kokangisa moto nzela ya kopanza.

src: In addition, the storage area is also equipped with a fire alarm system, so that if there is a fire, the alarm will sound and the fire department will be notified.
trg: Lisusu, esika ya kobomba biloko ezalaka mpe na alarme ya moto, mpo ete soki moto ebeli, alarme ekobeta mpe departema ya moto ekozwa liyebisi.

src: The storage area is also regularly inspected by the fire department, so that any potential fire hazards can be identified and addressed before they become a problem.
trg: Esika ya kobomba biloko departeme ya moto etalaka yango mbala na mbala mpo na komona likama ya moto oyo ekoki kozala mpe kolongola yango liboso ekoma likambo monene.

src: As a result of these measures, the storage area is a safe and secure place to store valuable goods.
trg: Miango oyo esalaka ete esika ya kobomba biloko ezala esika ya malamu mpo na kobomba biloko.

src: In addition to the fire safety measures, the storage area is also equipped with a security system to protect against theft.
trg: Longola miango oyo ya sécurité, esika ya kobomba biloko ezalaka mpe na ebongiseli ya sécurité mpo na komibatela na miyibi.

src: The security system consists of a surveillance camera, a burglar alarm, and a security guard.
trg: Ebongiseli ya sécurité ezalaka na kamera ya kokengela, alarme ya kobangisa miyibi mpe bakengeli.

src: The surveillance camera monitors the area 24 hours a day, the burglar alarm is activated if anyone tries to break in, and the security guard is on duty to patrol the area and respond to any incidents.
trg: Bakamera ya bokengi elandelaka esika wana bangonga 24 na mokolo, alarme ya kobangisa miyibi ebetaka soki moto nyonso ameki kokota, mpe bakengeli bazala na mosala ya kokengela esika wana mpe kosala mosala soki likambo ebimi.

src: As a result of these security measures, the storage area is a safe and secure place to store valuable goods.
trg: Miango oyo ya sécurité esalaka ete, bisika ya kobanda biloko ezalaka esika ya libateli mpeya malamu ya kobomba biloko.

src: Zambia is a landlocked country in Southern Africa.
trg: Zambie ezali mboka ekangama na Sude ya Afrika.

src: It is bordered by Angola to the west, the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the north, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi to the east, Mozambique to the southeast, Zimbabwe to the south, and Botswana to the southwest.
trg: Ekangama na Angola na weste, na Repiblike Demokratike ya Congo na norde, na Tanzanie na norde-este, na Malawi na este, na Mozambique na sude-este, na Zimbabwe na sude, mpe na Botswana na sude-weste.

src: Zambia has a population of over 17 million people and a land area of 752,618 square kilometers.
trg: Zambie ezali na bato koleka bamilio 17 mpe mabele na yango ezali monene na 752 618 kilometre carré.

src: Zambia's current president is Hakainde Hichilema, who was elected in August 2021.
trg: Prezida ya sikoyo ya Zambie ezali Hakainde Hichilema, oyo bavotaki ye na sanza ya Mwambe 2021.

src: Hichilema is a member of the United Party for National Development (UPND).
trg: Hichilema azali moto ya Parti ya Bomoko mpo na Bokoli ya Ekolo (UPND).

src: The UPND is the largest opposition party in Zambia.
trg: UPND ezali parti monene ya batelemeli na Zambie.

src: The economy of Zambia is based on copper mining.
trg: Ekonomi ya Zambie esimbami na kwivre.

src: Copper is the country's largest export.
trg: Kwivre ezali eleko ya ntina mingi oyo batekaka libanda ya mboka.

src: Other important exports include cobalt, zinc, and lead.
trg: Biloko mosusu ya ntina oyo batekaka libanda ya mboka ezali cobalt, zinc, mpe plomb.

src: The Zambian economy has been struggling in recent years due to low copper prices.
trg: Ekonomi ya Zambie ebunda makasi na mibu euti koleka mpo na bantalo ya nse ya kwivre.

src: Zambia is a member of the United Nations, the African Union, and the Southern African Development Community (SADC).
trg: Zambie ezali na kati ya Nations-Unies, ya Union Africaine, mpe ya Lisanga ya Bokoli ya Bikolo ya Afrika ya Sude (SADC).

src: A: I'm so itchy! I think I have lice.
trg: A: Nazali na mokusa makasi! Nakanisi nazali na sili.

src: B: Oh no! That's terrible.
trg: B: Oh te! Ezali likambo ya mabe.

src: I know how to get rid of them, though.
trg: Kasi, nayebi ndenge ya kolongola yango.

src: We can use a traditional remedy.
trg: Tokoki kosalela nkisi ya mboka.

src: A: What is it?
trg: A: Ezali nkisi nini?

src: B: We'll need some olive oil, some lemon juice, and a few cloves of garlic.
trg: B: Nazali na mposa ya ndambo ya mafuta ya olive, ndambo ya mai ya lilala, mpe ndambo ya ail.

src: A: Okay, I have all of that. What do we do with it?
trg: A: Malamu, nazali na biloko wana nyonso. Nakosala nini na yango?

src: B: First, we'll mix the olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic together.
trg: B: Ya liboso, tokosangisa mafuta ya olive, mai ya lilala, mpe ail.

src: Then, we'll apply it to your hair and scalp.
trg: Na nsima, tokotya yango na nsuki mpe na loposo ya moto na yo.

src: We'll let it sit for about an hour.
trg: Tokotika yango pene ya ngonga moko.

src: A: An hour? That sounds like a long time.
trg: A: Ngonga moko? Nazali komona neti ezali ntango ebele.

src: B: It is, but it's worth it.
trg: B: Ezali bongo, kasi ezali ntina.

src: The oil will help to suffocate the lice and the lemon juice will help to kill them.
trg: Mafuta ekosalisa na kokanga sili mpema mpe mai ya lilala ekosalisa na koboya ye.

src: The garlic will help to repel them.
trg: Ail ekosalisa na kobengama ye.

src: A: Okay, I'll do it.
trg: A: Malamu, nakosala yango.

src: "Mommy, what are those?" the toddler asked, pointing at the plants in the living room.
trg: "Mama, oyo nini?" mwana atunaki, azali kolakisa mosapi na banzete ezali na sallon.

src: "Those are plants," Mommy replied "They're living things, just like you and me."
trg: "Ezali banzete," wana eyano ya Mama "Ezali biloko ya bomoi, kaka neti yo na nga."

src: "Can I touch them?" the toddler asked.
trg: "Nakoki kosimba yango?" mwana atunaki.

src: "Yes, you can, but be gentle," Mommy said "The leaves are fragile."
trg: "Ee, okoki kosimba yango, kasi na boboto," Mama alobaki "Matiti ezali pete."

src: The toddler reached out and touched a leaf.
trg: Mwana asembolaki loboko mpe asimbaka nkasa.

src: The leaf felt soft and smooth.
trg: Nkasa ezalaki pete mpe muselu.

src: "I like it," the toddler said.
trg: "Nasepeli na yango," mwana alobaki.

src: "I'm glad," Mommy said. "Plants are good for us. They help clean the air and make us feel better."
trg: "Nasepeli," wana maloba ya Mama. "Banzete ezali malamu mpo na biso. Esalisaka na kopeto mopepe mpe esalaka tomiyoka malamu."

src: The toddler continued to look at the plants. Then, he noticed a cable running along the floor.
trg: Mwana akobaki kotala banzete. Na nsima, amonaki nsinga ya lotiliki ezali na mabele.

src: "What's that?" he asked.
trg: Atunaki, "Oyo nini?"

src: "That's a cable," Mommy said.
trg: Mama alobaki "Ezali nsinga ya lotiliki."

src: "It's used to connect the TV to the wall."
trg: "Tosalelaka yango mpo na kotya TV na efelo."

src: "Can I touch it?" the toddler asked.
trg: Mwana atunaki, "Nakoki kosimba yango?"

src: "No, you can't," Mommy said. "Cables can be dangerous.They can give you a shock."
trg: "Te, okoki kosimba yango te," wana maloba ya Mama. "Bansinga ya lotiliki ekoki kozala likama. Ekoki kolengisa yo."

src: The toddler looked disappointed, but he didn't touch the cable.
trg: Mwana alembaki nzoto, kasi asimbaki te nsinga ya lotiliki.

src: Person 1: Romantic Comedies are so unrealistic.
trg: Moto 1: Bateyatre ya Bolingo ezalaki lokuta mpenza.

src: Person 2: I know, right? The love interests always fall in love at first sight, and they never have any problems.
trg: Moto 2: Oyebi, bongo? Bato bazali na mposa ya kolinga balinganaka ntango nyonso na mbala ya liboso bakutani, bakutanaka ata na likambo moko te.

src: Person 1: And the conflicts are always so contrived.
trg: Moto 1: Mpe matata ezalaka kaka likololikolo.

src: Like, in one movie, the couple broke up because the guy's best friend was in love with the girl.
trg: Neti, na filme moko, babalani bakabwani mpo moninga ya makasi ya mobali azali na bolingo na mwana ya mwasi.

src: Person 2: That's so ridiculous. It's not like that happens in real life.
trg: Moto 2: Ezali bozoba mpenza. Esalemaka bongo te na bomoi ya solo.

src: Person 1: Exactly. And even when they do get together, it's always so perfect.
trg: Moto 1: Bongo mpenza. Mpe ata ntango bazali elongo, ezalaki ntango nyonso ya kokoka.

src: They never have any fights or disagreements.
trg: Babundaka te mpe bazalaka te na kozanga koyokana.

src: Person 2: It's like the movies are trying to tell us that love is always easy and perfect.
trg: Moto 2: Ezali neti filme ezali koluka koyebisa biso ete bolingo ezalaka ntango nyonso pete mpe ya kokoka.

src: But that's not the case.
trg: Kasi ezalaka bongo te.

src: Love is hard work.
trg: Bolingo ezali mosala makasi.

src: It takes time and effort to build a lasting relationship.
trg: Esengaka ntango mpe milende mpo na kosala boyokani oyo eumelaka.

src: Person 1: I know. That's why I don't watch rom-coms anymore.
trg: Moto 1: Nayebi. Yango wana natalaki lisusu te bateyatre ya bolingo.

src: They give people unrealistic expectations about love.
trg: Bapesaka bato makanisi ya lokuta mpo na bolingo.

src: My first day of school was a day I will never forget.
trg: Mokolo na nga ya liboso na eteyelo ezalaki mokolo nakotikala kobosana te.

src: I was both excited and nervous, not knowing what to expect.
trg: Nazalaki na esengo mpe motema likololikolo, nazalaki koyeba te ekozala ndenge nini.

src: When I woke up that morning, I got dressed quickly and ate a quick breakfast.
trg: Ntango nalamukaki na ntongo, nalataki noki mpe nalyaki na lombango.

src: Then, my mom drove me to school and walked me to my classroom.
trg: Na nsima, mama amemaki nga na eteyelo mpe amemaki nga na kelasi.

src: When I walked into the classroom, I was immediately greeted by my teacher, Ms. Smith.
trg: Ntango nakotaki na kelasi, na mbala moko molakisi, Madame Smith apesaki nga mbote.

src: She was a kind-looking woman with a warm smile.
trg: Azalaki mwana ya boboto oyo azalaki na koseka ya kitoko.

src: She introduced herself to me and then showed me to my seat.
trg: Ayebisaki nga nkombo na ye mpe na nsima apesaki nga esika ya kofanda.

src: I sat down next to a girl named Sarah.
trg: Nafandaka pene ya mwana-mwasi moko nkombo na ye Sarah.

src: She smiled at me and said, "Hi, I'm Sarah."
trg: Asekisaki nga mpe alobaki, "Mbote, nkombo na nga Sarah."

src: I smiled back and said, "Hi, I'm Vera."
trg: Nasekaki mpe, ebongo nalobaki, "Mbote, nkombo na nga Vera."

src: We talked for a few minutes before the bell rang for class to start.
trg: Tosololaki mwa miniti liboso ngonga ebeta mpo kelasi ebanda.

src: Ms. Smith began by introducing herself and telling us about the rules of the classroom.
trg: Madame Smith abandaki kopesa nkombo na ye mpe koyebisa biso mibeko ya kelasi.

src: Then, she started teaching us about math.
trg: Na nsima, abandaki koteya biso matematike.

src: I was a little bit confused at first, but Ms. Smith explained everything clearly.
trg: Nakamwaki mwa moke na ebandeli, kasi Madame Smith alimbolaki makambo nyonso na polele.

src: After math class, we had a break.
trg: Nsima ya mateya ya matematike, tozwaki bopemi.

src: Sarah and I went outside to play on the playground.
trg: Nga na Sarah tokendaki libanda mpo na kosakana.

src: We played on the swings and the slide for a while, then we went back inside for lunch.
trg: Tosakanaki na badyemba mwa moke, na nsima tokotaki na kati mpo na kolya ya midi.

src: When tissue is injured, the body’s immune system sends white blood cells to the area.
trg: Soki tissue ezoki, systeme immunitaire ya nzoto etindaka baselile ya mpembe ya makila na esika wana.

src: These cells release chemicals that cause blood vessels to dilate and become more permeable.
trg: Baselile oyo ebimisaka biloko ya chimie oyo esalaka ete misisa ya makila ekoma minene mpe elekisa biloko.

src: This allows fluid and white blood cells to leak out of the blood vessels and into the injured tissue.
trg: Epesaka nzela mpo mai mpe baselile ya mpembe ya makila ebima na misisa ya makila mpe ekota na mpota.

src: The fluid forms a clear, watery swelling called edema.
trg: Mai wana esalaka kovimba ya polele mpe ya maimai babengi oedeme.

src: The white blood cells help to fight infection and to remove damaged tissue.
trg: Baselile ya mpembe ya makila esalisaka na kobundisa maladi mpe na kolongola tissue oyo ebebi.

src: They also release chemicals that stimulate the growth of new tissue.
trg: Ebimisaka mpe biloko ya chimie oyo elendisaka bokoli ya tissue ya sika.

src: The classic signs of acute inflammation are redness, heat, swelling, and pain.
trg: Bilembo eyebana mingi ya mpasi ya makasi ezali motane, moto, kovimba, mpe mpasi.

src: These signs are caused by the increased blood flow and the release of chemicals in the injured tissue.
trg: Bilembo oyo eutaka na ndenge makila ekomi kotambola mingi mpe na kobimisama ya biloko ya chime na tissue oyo ezoki.

src: Redness is caused by the dilation of blood vessels.
trg: Motane eutaka na ndenge bavaisseau ya makila ekomaka monene.

src: Heat is caused by the increased blood flow and the release of inflammatory chemicals.
trg: Moto eutaka na ndenge makila ekomi kotambola migi mpe na kobimisama ya biloko ya chimie.

src: Swelling is caused by the leakage of fluid from blood vessels into the injured tissue.
trg: Kovimba eutaka na kobima ya mai na bavaisseau ya makila mpo ekota na tissue oyo ezoki.

src: Pain is caused by the release of inflammatory chemicals and the pressure of the swelling.
trg: Mpasi eutaka na kobimisama ya biloko ya chimie mpe na pression oyo ezala na kovimba.

src: Acute inflammation is a normal part of the healing process.
trg: Mpasi ya makasi ezali eteni ya ntina ya kobika.

src: However, if it is severe or prolonged, it can damage healthy tissue.
trg: Kasi, ezali ya makasi mingi to ezali kosila te, ekoki kobebisa tissue ya malamu.

src: In some cases, acute inflammation can lead to chronic inflammation, which is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
trg: Na bandakisa mosusu mpasi ya makasi ekoki komema mpasi oyo esilaka te, oyo ezali maladi oyo ekoki kopesa mpasi, ebosono, to kutu liwa.

src: There are a number of things that can cause acute inflammation, including infection, injury, and autoimmune diseases.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo ekoki kobimisa mpasi ya makasi, neti maladi, mpota, mpe bokono ya auto-immune.

src: Infections are caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.
trg: Maladi eutaka na mikrobe, bavirisi, to bachampignon.

src: When these organisms enter the body, they can trigger an immune response that leads to inflammation.
trg: Soki biloko wana ekoti na nzoto, ekoki kotinda nzoto na kobundisa yango ebona ekoki kobimisa mpasi.

src: Injuries can also cause inflammation.
trg: Bampota ekoki mpe kobimisa mpasi.

src: When tissue is damaged, it releases chemicals that attract white blood cells and other immune cells to the area.
trg: Soki tissue ebebi, ebimisaka biloko ya chimie oyo ebendaka baselile ya mpembe ya makila mpe baselile mosusu ya esika wana.

src: These cells release chemicals that cause inflammation.
trg: Baselila oyo ebimisaka biloko ya chimie oyo ebimisaka mpasi.

src: Autoimmune diseases are caused by the body’s immune system attacking its own tissues.
trg: Maladi ya auto-immune ebimaka ntango systeme immunitaire ya nzoto ebundisaka ba tissue na yango moko.

src: This can lead to inflammation in the affected tissues.
trg: Ekoki komema na mpasi oyo ezalaka na bopusi na ba tissue.

src: Acute inflammation is usually treated with pain relievers, such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen.
trg: Mbala mingi mpasi ya makasi esilaka soki ozwi nkisi oyo esilisaka mpasi, neti ibuprofen to acetaminophene.

src: In some cases, corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation.
trg: Na bandakisa mosusu, bakoki kosalela corticosteroide mpo na kokitisa mpasi.

src: If the inflammation is caused by an infection, antibiotics may be prescribed.
trg: Soki mpasi euti na maladi, bakoki kokomela yo ba antibiotique.

src: Chronic inflammation is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
trg: Mpasi oyo ezali kosila te ezali maladi ya ntango moali oyo ekoki komema mpasi, ebosono, to nkutu liwa.

src: It is often caused by autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease.
trg: Eutaka mbala mingi na maladi ya auto-immune, neti polyarthrite rymatoide mpe maladi ya Crohn.

src: Chronic inflammation can also be caused by obesity, smoking, and air pollution.
trg: Mpasi esilaka te ekoki kouta na ndenge ozali monene makasi, makaya, mpe kobeba ya mopepe.

src: There is no cure for chronic inflammation, but it can be managed with medication, lifestyle changes, and physical therapy.
trg: Ezali te na nkisi mpo na kobikisa mpasi oyo esilaka te, kasi nkisi, mbongwana ya lolenge ya bomoi mpe ngalasisi ekoki kosalisa.

src: The Mozambican Civil War was a conflict that lasted from 1977 to 1992.
trg: Bitumba ya Bana-Mboka ya Mozambique ezali bitumba oyo ebandaki na 1977 kino na 1992.

src: It was fought between the Mozambique Liberation Front (FRELIMO), which had ruled the country since its independence from Portugal in 1975, and the Mozambique National Resistance (RENAMO), a rebel group backed by the Rhodesian and South African governments.
trg: Ebundamaki kati ya Lisanga ya Lipanda ya Mozambique (FRELIMO), oyo ezalaki koyangela mboka banda na lipanda na yango na Portugal na 1975, mpe Lisanga ya Botemeli ya Mozambique (RENAMO), etulu ya batomboki oyo ezalaki na lisungi ya boyangeli ya Rodésie mpe ya Afrike du Sude.

src: The war caused widespread devastation and displacement, and led to the deaths of an estimated 1 million people.
trg: Bitumba wana ebebisaki biloko ebele mpe bato ebele bakimaki mboka, mpe ebomaki bato mingi pene ya milio 1.

src: The war began after RENAMO launched an insurgency against FRELIMO in 1977.
trg: Bitumba ebandaka ntango RENAMO ebandaki kobundisa FRELIMO na 1977.

src: RENAMO was opposed to FRELIMO's socialist policies and its close ties to the Soviet Union.
trg: RENAMO ezalaki kotelemela mibeko ya sociale ya FRELIMO mpe boyokani na yango ya makasi na Union Sovietique.

src: The war quickly escalated, and by the early 1980s, RENAMO had control of much of the countryside.
trg: Bitumba ekomaka makasi noki, mpe na ebandeli ya mibu 1980, RENAMO ekomaki koyangela bamboka mingi.

src: FRELIMO was forced to rely on Soviet and Cuban military aid to keep RENAMO at bay.
trg: FRELIMO ezwaki lisungi basoda ya Union Sovietique mpe ya Cuba mpo na kobatela RENAMO mosika.

src: In 1984, FRELIMO and RENAMO signed a peace agreement, but the fighting continued.
trg: Na 1984, FRELIMO na RENAMO batyaki maboko na boyokani ya kimya, kasi bitumba ekobaki.

src: In 1992, the two sides signed a new peace agreement, which called for a ceasefire and the holding of multiparty elections.
trg: Na 1992, bituluku mibale wana etyaki maboko na boyokani ya kimya, oyo esangaki basilisa masasi mpe basala vote ya baparti ebele.

src: My friend, Abel, and I were walking home from school one day when we saw a blood drive being held at our local community center.
trg: Moninga na nga Abel, na nga tozalaki kozonga na ndako nsima ya kouta na kelasi mokolo moko mpe tomonaki bazali komema na lopitalo moko ya kartie mokumbi-motuka oyo azokaki.

src: We were both 17 years old, and we had never donated blood before.
trg: Biso mibale tozali na mibu 17, mpe totikala nanu te kopesa makila na biso libonza.

src: We decided to stop in and see what it was all about.
trg: Tozwaki ekateli ya kotelema mpe kotala soki ezalaki mpenza nini.

src: The process of donating blood was actually pretty simple.
trg: Ndenge basalaka makambo mpo na kopesa makila ezalaki mpenza pete.

src: We both filled out a questionnaire and answered some questions about our health history.
trg: Biso mibale totondisaki mituna mpe toyanolaki ndambo ya mituna etali kolongono ya nzoto na biso.

src: Then, we had our blood pressure checked and our veins were checked to make sure they were big enough.
trg: Na nsima, batalaki tension na biso mpe batalaki misisa na biso mpo na koyeba soki ezalaki mpenza minene.

src: Once we were cleared to donate, we each sat down in a chair and had a needle inserted into our arms.
trg: Ntango bandimaki ete topesa makila, biso mibale tofandaki na kiti mpe bakotisaki ntonda na maboko na biso.

src: The blood was collected in a bag, and the whole process took about 15 minutes.
trg: Bazwaki makila na saki moko, mpe makambo nyonso wana ezwaki miniti pene ya 15.

src: It felt good to know that we were helping to save lives.
trg: Namiyokaki malamu na koyeba ete tozalaki kosalisa na kobikisa bato.

src: After we donated, we were given a juice box and a cookie to help us recover.
trg: Nsima ya kopesa makila, bapesaki biso molangi ya jus mpe biscuit mpo na kosalisa biso na kozongisa makasi.

src: We also received a thank-you card from the blood bank.
trg: Bapesaki biso mpe karte ya kado ya kopesa matondi euti na banki ya makila.

src: I'm glad that Abel and I decided to donate blood.
trg: Nazali na esengo mpo nga na Abel tozwaki ekateli ya kopesa makila.

src: It was a quick and easy way to make a difference in the world.
trg: Ezalaki lolenge ya noki mpe ya pete ya kosala bokeseni na mokili.

src: I encourage everyone to consider donating blood if they are eligible.
trg: Nazali kolendisa moto nyonso na kotala soki akoki kopesa makila soki akokisi masengami.

src: It's a simple act of kindness that can help save lives.
trg: Ezali likambo ya pete ya boboto oyo ekoki kosalisa na kobikisa bato.

src: A solo traveler was found safe after spending two nights lost in the Swiss Alps.
trg: Bamonaki mosali-mobembo moko oyo azalaki kosala mobembo ye moko malamu nsima ya kolekisa butu mibale ya kobunga na ba Alpes ya Suisse.

src: The 25-year-old woman, who has not been identified, was hiking in the mountains when she became separated from her group.
trg: Mwana-mwasi ya mibu 25, oyo bayebaki ye te, azalaki kotambola na bangomba ntango akabwanaki na etuluku na ye.

src: She was reported missing on Tuesday, and search teams were dispatched to find her.
trg: Balobaki na mokolo ya mibale ete abungi, mpe batindaki bituluku ya koluka mpo na kokende koluka ye.

src: The woman was eventually found on Thursday, about 10 miles from where she had been hiking.
trg: Nsukansuka bamonaki mwasi wana na mokolo ya Minei, pene ya 10 miles na esika oyo abandaki kotambola.

src: She was cold and dehydrated, but otherwise in good condition.
trg: Azalaki na malili mpe alembi mpo amelaki mai te, kasi longola yango azalaki malamu.

src: She told rescuers that she had been following a trail when she got turned around.
trg: Ayebisaki bato oyo babikisaki ye ete azalaki kolanda nzela moko ntango abalukaki.

src: She spent the night in a cave, and she survived by eating snow and drinking from a stream.
trg: Alekisaka butu na libulu, mpe abikaki na kolyaka neze mpe komela na mai oyo ezalaki koleka.

src: The woman's experience is a reminder of the importance of being prepared when hiking in the mountains.
trg: Makambo mwasi wana akutanaki na yango ezali kokundwela biso ntina ya komibongisa ntango ozali kotambola na bangomba.

src: Hikers should always bring a map, compass, and a flashlight, and they should tell someone where they are going and when they expect to return.
trg: Bato batambolaka na bangomba bamemaka ntango nyonso karte, bussole, mpe torshe, mpe basengeli koyebisa moto moko ete bakei mpe ntango oyo bakanisi bakozonga.

src: The debate about whether animals are happier in the wild or in zoos is a complex one with no easy answers.
trg: Koswana ya koluka koyeba soki banyama bazalaka na esengo na zamba to na zoo ezali ya mpasi mpe ezali te na eyano ya pete.

src: There are many factors to consider, including the individual animal's needs, the type of zoo, and the quality of care provided.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele ya kotalela, neti bamposa ya nyama mokomoko, lolenge ya zoo, mpe ndenge bazali kobatela yango.

src: Some animals, such as elephants, are highly social and need to interact with other elephants in order to thrive.
trg: Banyama mosusu, neti banzoko, esepealaka mpenza kofanda na basusu mpe elingaka kozala na banzoko mosusu mpo na kozala malamu.

src: In the wild, elephants live in herds of up to 100 individuals.
trg: Na zamba, banzoko bafandaka na bituluku ya banzoko kino na 100.

src: They spend their days foraging for food, playing, and socializing.
trg: Balekisaka mikolo na koluka bilei, na kosakana mpe kozala elongo.

src: In a zoo, elephants may not have the same opportunities to interact with other elephants, which can lead to boredom and frustration.
trg: Na zoo, mbala mosusu banzoko bakoki te kozala na mabaku ya kozala elongo na banzoko mosusu, likambo oyo ekoki kolembisa mpe kosilisaka bango.

src: Other animals, such as lions, are solitary hunters.
trg: Banyama mosusu, neti bankosi, bakilaka bango moko.

src: In the wild, lions live in prides of up to 15 individuals.
trg: Na zamba, bankosi bafandaka na bituluku ya bankosi kino na 15.

src: However, each lion within the pride has its own territory and does not interact with other lions very often.
trg: Kasi, nkosi nyonso na kati ya etuluku azali na teritware na ye mpe akutanaka te na bankosi mosusu mbala na mbala.

src: In a zoo, lions may be able to live in larger enclosures with more space to roam, which can provide them with more opportunities to exercise and explore.
trg: Na zoo, bankosi bakoki kofanda na mapangu ya minene esika na espace mingi ya kotambola, oyo ekoki kopesa bango mabaku ebele ya kosala ngalasisi mpe kotambola.

src: The type of zoo also plays a role in the welfare of its animals.
trg: Lolenge ya zoo ezalaka mpe na mokumba mpo na bolamu ya banyama na yango.

src: Some zoos are very large and provide their animals with spacious enclosures, while others are smaller and may not have as much space.
trg: Bazoo mosusu ezalaki minene mpenza mpe epesaka banyama na yango mapango ya minene, kasi mosusu ezalaka moke mpenza mpe mbala mosusu ezali te na esika mingi.

src: As I'm driving down the road, I see a goat giving birth in the median.
trg: Ntango nazali kokumba na nzela, namoni ntaba azali kobota na katikati.

src: She's lying on her side and her two front legs are extended in front of her.
trg: Alali na mopanzi mpe makolo na ye mibale ebendami na liboso na ye.

src: The baby goat is coming out of her right side and it's head is already visible.
trg: Mwana ya ntaba azali kobima na ndambo ya loboko ya mobali mpe moto na ye ezali komonana.

src: The mother goat looks up at me and I can see the fear in her eyes.
trg: Mama ya ntaba atalaki nga mpe nakokaki komona bobangi na miso na ye.

src: She's probably wondering if I'm going to hurt her or her baby.
trg: Mbala mosusu azali komituna soki nakosale ye to bebe na ye mabe.

src: I stop the car and get out.
trg: Nakangi motuka mpe nabimi.

src: I walk over to the goat and kneel down next to her.
trg: Nakei epai ntaba azali mpe nagumbami pene na ye.

src: I gently stroke her head and tell her that everything is going to be okay.
trg: Nasimbi moto na ye na boboto mpe nayebisi ye ete makambo nyonso ekosimba.

src: The baby goat starts to emerge and I can see that it's a little girl.
trg: Mwana ya ntaba abandi kobima mpe nakoki komona ezali mwana-ntaba ya moke.

src: She's crying and her mother licks her clean.
trg: Ezali kolela mpe mama alemboli ye mpo na kosukola ye.

src: I watch as the mother goat and baby bond and I feel a sense of peace.
trg: Natali ntango mama ya ntaba na bebe bazali koyokana mpe nayoki kimya moko boye.

src: Demonetization is the process of removing legal tender from circulation.
trg: Demonetisation ezali mosala ya kosilisa ngala na mbongo oyo bazali kosalela.

src: In India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on November 8, 2016, that all ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes would cease to be legal tender from midnight.
trg: Na Inde, Ministre ya Yambo Narendra Modi alobaki na mokolo ya 8 sanza ya Zomi na Moke 2016 ete ba ₹500 mpe ba ₹1000 nyonso ekozala lisusu na ngala te banda na minuit.

src: This move was intended to crack down on corruption and counterfeiting, but it also caused significant disruption and hardship for many people.
trg: Mokano na yandi ezalaki ya kokanga nzela na avoka mpe mbongo ya lokuta, kasi ememelaki mpe bato ebele bampasi mpe mikakatano ya makasi.

src: There are several reasons to be skeptical of demonetization.
trg: Ezali na bantina ebele ya kondimela te demonetisation.

src: First, it is not clear that it will be effective in reducing corruption.
trg: Ya liboso, eyebani te polele ete ekokoba mpenza kokitisa avoka.

src: Corruption is a complex problem that cannot be solved simply by removing cash from circulation.
trg: Avoka ezali likambo ya mpasi oyo bakoki kosilisa te kaka na kosilisa mbongo ngala.

src: In fact, there is some evidence that demonetization may actually increase corruption, as it makes it more difficult for people to track and trace their money.
trg: Ya solo, ezali na mwa bilembeteli ezali komonisa ete demonetisation ekoki mpenza kokitisa avoka, mpo ekomaka mpasi mpo bato balandela mbongo na bango.

src: Second, demonetization is likely to have a negative impact on the poor.
trg: Ya mibale, demonetisation ekoki kozala na bopusi ya mabe na babola.

src: Many poor people in India rely on cash for their daily transactions.
trg: Babola ebele ya Inde bazalaka na mposa ya mbongo na maboko mpo na kosala misala.

src: The sudden withdrawal of large-denomination banknotes made it difficult for them to buy food, pay their bills, and access other essential services.
trg: Kosilisa na mbala moko mbongo ebele ngala na nzela ya demonetisation esalaki ete ezala mpasi mpo babola basomba bilei, bafuta bafaktire, mpe bazwa misala ya ntina.

src: Third, demonetization has caused significant disruption to the economy.
trg: Ya misato, demonetisation ekotisa nkokoso ya makasi na ekonomi.

src: Businesses had to close for days or even weeks while they adjusted to the new currency.
trg: Mimbongo esengeli kokanga mikolo to kutu bamposo ebele ntango bazali komesana na mbongo ya sika.

src: The dish is said to have originated in the Philippines, where it is known as lechon.
trg: Balobaka ete elubu wana euta na Philipines, esika babengaka yango lechon.

src: It is also popular in other parts of Southeast Asia, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
trg: Eyebana mpe mingi na bisika mosusu ya Sude-este ya Asie, neti na Indonensie, Malysie, mpe Thailande.

src: To make lechon, a whole pig is gutted and cleaned, then stuffed with a mixture of garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and other spices.
trg: Mpo na kolamba lechon, babomaki ngulu mobimba mpe basokolaka yango, na nsima bakolaki yango ail, tangawisi, matiti ya malala mpe biloko mosusu.

src: The pig is then roasted over a fire of charcoal or wood for several hours.
trg: Na nsima batumbaka ngulu na moto ya makala to ya nkoni na boumeli ya mwa bangonga.

src: The result is a juicy, flavorful meat that is perfect for a special occasion.
trg: Ebimisaka mosuni ya kitoko makasi oyo ebongi mpo na libaku ya speciale.

src: Lechon is often served with rice and vegetables.
trg: Mbala mingi balyaka lechon na loso mpe bandunda.

src: It can also be eaten as a main course or as an appetizer.
trg: Ekoki kolyama mpe lokola bilei ya monene to biloko ya kosepelisa monoko.

src: If you are ever lucky enough to try lechon, you will not be disappointed.
trg: Soki ozali na chance ya komeka kolya lechon, okolemba nzoto ata moke te.

src: It is truly a unique and delicious dish.
trg: Ezali mpenza elubu ya malamu mpe ya kitoko.

src: In addition to the traditional method of cooking lechon, there are also several modern variations.
trg: Longola lolenge ya kala ya kolamba lechon, ezali na balolenge mosusu ya lelo ya kosala yango.

trg: Mobange ya Mobali mpe Mbu

trg: Santiago, molobi-mbisi ya kala ya Cuba, asalaki mikolo ntuku mwame kozanga kokanga mbisi.

src: He is the oldest man in the village, and the youngest, Manolin, no longer wants to fish with him because the old man is unlucky.

src: One day, Santiago sets out in his skiff and hooks a giant marlin.
trg: Mokolo moko, Santiago akei na bwatu na ye ya moke mpe akangi marlin ya monene.

trg: Marlin yango ezali monene mingi yango wana ememi bwatu mosika na mbu.

src: Santiago fights the marlin for two days and nights, but he cannot bring it in.
trg: Santiago abundi na marlin moi mpe butu mibale, kasi akoki te kobimisa yango libanda.

src: The marlin is too heavy, and the old man is too tired.

trg: Kasi marlin ezali monene mingi yango wana Santiago akoki te kokotisa yango na bwatu.

src: He ties the marlin to the side of the boat and begins to row back to shore.
trg: Akangi marlin na mopanzi ya bwatu mpe abandi koluka mpo na kozonga na mokili.

trg: Etuluku ya barequin ezali kolanda maswa, mpe babandi kolya marlin.

src: By the time he reaches shore, only the head and the tail of the marlin are left.
trg: Ntango akomi na mokili, kaka moto na mokila ya marlin nde etikali.

src: The police will likely take the person to the station and question him.
trg: Bapolisi basengeli mpenza komema moto wana na biro mpe kotuna ya mituna.
