src: The history of Cameroon is long and complex, dating back to the earliest human settlements in the region.
trg: Lisolo ya Cameroun ezali ya molai mpe ya mpasi, ebanda na banda bato bafanda kala na etuka wana.

src: The area was first settled by Bantu peoples around 3000 BCE, and it was later conquered by the Kanem-Bornu Empire in the 11th century.
trg: Bato bazalaki nanu wana ezalaki ba Bantu pene ya 3000 Liboso ya Ntango na Biso, mpe na nsima Bokonzi ya Kanem-Bornu ebotolaki yango na ekeke ya 11.

src: In the 15th century, the Portuguese arrived in Cameroon and established trade relations with the local people.
trg: Na ekeke ya 15, bato ya Portugal bakomaki na Cameroun mpe babandisaki mombongo na bana ya mboka.

src: The region was later colonized by Germany in the 1880s, and it became a German colony known as Kamerun.
trg: Etuka wana eyangelamaki na bato ya nkanza ya Allemagne na mibu 1880, mpe ekomaki na nse ya bokonzi ya Allemange na nkombo ya Kamerun.

src: During World War I, Cameroon was occupied by British and French forces, and it was divided between the two countries after the war.
trg: Na Bitumba ya Liboso ya Mokili Mobimba, basoda ya Grande-Bretagne na France ebotolaki Cameroun, mpe bakabolaki yango bango mibale nsima ya bitumba.

src: The British-controlled region became known as Southern Cameroons, while the French-controlled region became known as French Cameroon.
trg: Eteni oyo Grande-Bretagne ezalaki koyangeli ebengamaki Cameroun ya Sude, mpe eteni oyo France ezalaki koyangela ebengamaki Cameroun ya France.

src: In 1960, Southern Cameroons became independent from Britain, and it merged with French Cameroon to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon.
trg: Na 1960, Cameroun ya Sude ezwaki lipanda na Grande-Bretagne, mpe esanganaki na Cameroun ya France mpo na kosala Ekolo Federale ya Cameroun.

src: In 1972, the federal system was abolished and Cameroon became a unitary state.
trg: Na 1972, babomaki ebongiseli ya federal mpe Cameroun ekomaki ekolo moko.

src: Cameroon has experienced a number of political and economic challenges in recent years.
trg: Cameroun ekutana na bampasi ebele ya politiki mpe ya ekonomi na bambula euti koleka.

src: Trimming your dog's nails is a necessary part of grooming, but it can be a daunting task for some pet owners.
trg: Kokata manzaka ya mbwa na yo ezali eteni ya ntina ya monzele na ye, kasi ekoki kozala mosala ya mpasi mpo na bankolo bambwa mosusu.

src: If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, don't worry - it's easier than you think.
trg: Soki oyebi te ndenge ya kokata manzaka ya mbwa na yo, komitungisa te - ezali pete koleka ndenge ozali kokanisa.

src: The first step is to gather your supplies.
trg: Etape ya liboso ezali ya kozwa bisaleli.

src: You'll need a pair of sharp scissors or a nail clipper, a styptic powder or pencil, and a towel.
trg: Okozala na mposa ya ba ciseaux ya mpya to ekateli manzaka, poudre styptique to crayon, mpe elamba.

src: Next, you'll need to clip your dog's nails in a comfortable place.
trg: Na nsima, osengeli kokata manzaka ya mbwa na yo na esika ya malamu.

src: If your dog is nervous, try clipping their nails in a quiet room where they can't see out the window.
trg: Soki mbwa na yo azali na nkanda, meka kokata manzaka na ye na esika ya kimya esika akoki kotala na fenetre.

src: You may also want to have someone help you hold your dog still.
trg: Okoki kolinga mpe ete moto mosusu asunga yo na kokanga mbwa aningana te.

src: To trim your dog's nails, start by gently grasping their paw.
trg: Mpo na kokata manzaka ya mbwa, banda na kosimba makolo na ye na boboto.

src: Then, use your scissors or clippers to clip the tip of the nail.
trg: Na nsima, salela ba ciseaux to bikateli manzaka mpo na kokata nsonge ya linzaka.

src: Be careful not to cut too short, as this can cause pain and bleeding.
trg: Kokata yango te mikuse makasi, mpo ekoki kopesa ye mpasi mpe kobimisa makila.

src: If you do cut your dog's nail too short, apply a styptic powder or pencil to stop the bleeding.
trg: Soki okati manzaka ya mbwa na yo mikuse mpenza, salela poudre styptique to crayon mpo na kokanga makila oyo ezali kobima.

src: Styptic powders and pencils are available at most pet stores.
trg: Bapoudre ya styptique mpe ba crayon ezalaka na babutiki ebele ya banyama.

src: Once you've trimmed all of your dog's nails, be sure to reward them with a treat.
trg: Soki osilisi kokata manzaka nyonso ya mbwa na yo, kobosana te kopesa ye mwa bilei.

src: Trimming nails can be a stressful experience for some dogs, so it's important to make it a positive experience.
trg: Kokata manzaka ekoki kozala lkambo ya mpasi mpo na bambwa mosusu, yango wana ezali ntina osala ezali likambo ya malamu.

src: With a little practice, you'll be able to trim your dog's nails like a pro.
trg: Na komeka mwa moke, okokoka kokata manzaka ya mbwa lokola moto ayebi mosala.

src: And your dog will be happy to have their nails trimmed, too!
trg: Mpe mbwa na yo akozala na esengo ya kozala na manzaka na ye ya kokata mpe!

src: Here are a few additional tips for trimming your dog's nails:
trg: Tala mwa batoli mosusu mpo na kokata manzaka ya mbwa na yo:

src: * Start by trimming the nails on your dog's front paws.
trg: * Banda kokata manzaka ya mbwa na yo na makolo ya liboso.

src: This is usually the easiest place to start.
trg: Mbala mingi ezalaka esika ya pete ya kobanda.

src: * If your dog is nervous, try trimming their nails one at a time.
trg: * Soki mbwa azali na nkanda, meka kokata linzaka moko na mbala moko.

src: * Be sure to trim the nails evenly.
trg: * Sala nyonso okata manzaka ndenge moko.

src: You don't want one nail to be shorter than the others.
trg: Olingi te linzaka moko ezala mokuse koleka mosusu.

src: * If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, ask your veterinarian or a groomer for help.
trg: * Soki oyebi te ndenge ya kokata manzaka ya mbwa, senga monganga na yo ya banyama to mosali ya kobongisa nzoto na kosalisa yo.

src: With a little care and attention, you can keep your dog's nails trimmed and healthy.
trg: Soki otye mwa likebi mpe okipe moke, okoki kosalisa na kobatela manzaka ya mbwa ya kokata mpe malamu.

src: Ivory Coast is a country in West Africa that has been in the midst of a civil war since 2010.
trg: Côte d'Ivoire ezali mboka ya Afrika ya Weste oyo bazala na bitumba ya bana-mboka banda 2010.

src: The conflict began after incumbent president Laurent Gbagbo refused to accept defeat in the 2010 presidential election.
trg: Bitumba ebandaki nsima wana Laurent Gbagbo prezida azalaki na bokonzi aboyaki kondima kopola na ye na maponi ya prezida ya 2010.

src: Gbagbo was eventually ousted by forces loyal to Alassane Ouattara, who was declared the winner of the election.
trg: Nsukansuka Gbagbo abenganamaki na basoda oyo bazalaki kopesa Alassane Ouattare, oyo azalaki molongi ya maponi wana.

src: However, the conflict has continued, with sporadic violence breaking out in the country.
trg: Kasi, bitumba ekobaki, mpe mobulu ya makasi ekotaka na mboka.

src: In 2017, there were hopes that the country would finally be able to move on from the civil war.
trg: Na 2017, elikya ezalaki ete nsukansuka mboka akosilisa bitumba na yango kati ya bana-mboka.

src: However, these hopes were dashed when Gbagbo was acquitted of charges of crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court.
trg: Kasi, bilikya wana ebebaka ntango Tribinale Internantionale ya Crime ekweisaki bifundeli ya ba crime contre l'humanité oo bafundaki Gbagbo.

src: Gbagbo's acquittal was seen as a blow to the peace process, and it led to renewed violence in the country.
trg: Kokweisa bifundeli ya Gbagbo ezalaki eloko ya mabe mpo na makambo ya kimya, mpe ezongisaki mobulu na mboka.

src: In 2018, the United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions on Gbagbo and his supporters.
trg: Na 2018, Conseil ya Sécurité ya Nations-Unies epesaki Gbagbo na bato na ye bitumbu.

src: The sanctions were aimed at pressuring Gbagbo to end his support for violence in the country.
trg: Mokano ya bitumbu wana ezalaki ya kopusa Gbagbo na kotika kopesa maboko na mobulu na mboka.

src: The sanctions have had some success, and there has been a decrease in violence in Ivory Coast since they were imposed.
trg: Bitumbu wana elonga mwa moke, mpe mobulu ekita moke na Côte d'Ivoire banda bapesa yango.

src: However, the country is still far from stable.
trg: Kasi, mboka ezali kaka mosika ya kozwa kimya.

src: In the beginning, there was only darkness.
trg: Na ebandeli, ezalaki kaka molili.

src: The universe was a vast, empty void.
trg: Molongo ezalaki monene mpe mpamba.

src: Then, out of the darkness, came a spark.
trg: Na nsima, na kati ya molili, mwa pole ebimaki.

src: This spark was the first sign of life in the universe.
trg: Mwa pole wana ezalaki elembo ya liboso ya bomoi na molongo.

src: It grew and expanded, becoming a small ball of fire.
trg: Ekomaki mingi mpe epanzanaki, ekomaki mwa boule moko ya moto.

src: This ball of fire was the sun.
trg: Boule wana ya moto ezalaki moi.

src: Around the sun, the planets began to form.
trg: Zingazinga ya moi, baplanete ebandaki kosalema.

src: The Earth was the third planet from the sun.
trg: Mabele ezalaki planete ya misato na moi.

src: It was a small, rocky planet with a thin atmosphere.
trg: Ezalaki moke, planete ya mabangamabanga oyo ezalaki na atmosphere ya moke.

src: On the Earth, the first living things began to appear.
trg: Na Mabele, ekelamu ya liboso ya bomoi ebandaki komonana.

src: These were simple organisms, such as bacteria and algae.
trg: Ezalaki na biloko ya mike, neti bamikrobe mpe algue.

src: Over time, these organisms evolved into more complex forms of life, such as plants and animals.
trg: Na nsima, biloko wana ya mike ekomaki lolenge ya bomoi ya kokamwa, neti banzete mpe banyama.

src: The first humans appeared on Earth about 200,000 years ago.
trg: Bato ya liboso bamonanaki na Mabele pene ya mibu 200 000 eleki.

src: Humans have evolved and developed to become the dominant species on Earth.
trg: Bato bakolaki mpe balekaki bikelamu nyonso na Mabele.

src: The universe is still expanding and evolving.
trg: Molongo ezali kokoba kokoma monene mpe kobongwana.

src: Scientists believe that it will continue to expand for billions of years.
trg: Bato ya siansi bakanisaka ete ekokoba kokoma monene na bamiliare ya bambula.

src: Eventually, the universe will reach a point where it can no longer expand.
trg: Nsukansuka, molongo ekokoma na esika oyo ekokoka lisusu te kokoma monene.

src: At this point, the universe will begin to contract.
trg: Na ntango wana, molongo ekobanda kokonda.

src: Eventually, the universe will collapse in on itself and disappear.
trg: Nsukansuka, molonga ekopanzana yango moko mpe ekolimwa.

src: But even though the universe may end, the story of life will continue.
trg: Kasi ata soki molngo ekoki kosuka, lisolo ya bomoi ekokoba.

src: The old wooden boat sat on the shore, its sails furled and its hull weathered by the sun and the rain.
trg: Masuwa ya kala ya mabaya efandaki na libongo, bavoile na yango ezalaki ya kobaluka mpe coque na yango ebebaki na moi mpe mbula.

src: It had seen many years of service, carrying its owners on voyages to far-off lands.
trg: Esila komona bambula ebele ya misala, ememaka bankolo na yango na mibembo na mikili ya mosika mpenza.

src: But now, it was retired, its days of sailing over.
trg: Kasi sikoyo, esalaka lisusu te, mikolo na yango ya kosala esila.

src: One day, a young boy named Thomas came to the beach.
trg: Mokolo moko, elenge mobali moko na nkombo ya Thomas ayaki na libongo.

src: He had heard stories about the old boat, and he was eager to see it for himself.
trg: Ayokaki masolo ya maswa wana ya kala, mpe azalaki na mposa makasi ya komona yango ye moko.

src: When he saw the boat, he was amazed by its size and its beauty.
trg: Ntango amonaki maswa wana, monene mpe kitoko na yango ekamwisaki.

src: He could imagine himself sailing off on adventures in the vast ocean.
trg: Azalaki kokanisa azali komema yango na mobembo na mbu ya monene.

src: Thomas asked the owner of the boat if he could take a closer look.
trg: Thomas atunaka nkolo-masuwa soki akoki kotala yango na pene.

src: The owner smiled and said, "Of course you can. Come aboard!"
trg: Nkolo na yango asekaki mpe alobaki, "Likambo te okoki kotala yango. Yaka komata!"

src: Thomas climbed into the boat and sat down in the captain's chair.
trg: Thomas akotaki na masuwa mpe afandaka na kiti ya kapitene.

src: He looked out over the water and imagined himself sailing away to a faraway land.
trg: Atalaki likolo ya mai mpe akanisaka ye moko azali komema yango mokili moko ya mosika.

src: The owner of the boat watched Thomas for a moment, then said, "Do you want to learn how to sail?"
trg: Nkolo-masuwa atalaki Thomas mwa ntango, na nsima alobaki, "Ozali kolinga koyekola ndenge ya komema masuwa?"

src: Thomas' eyes widened "Yes" he said.
trg: Miso ya Thomas efungwamaki mpe alobaki "Ee."

src: The owner of the boat smiled again.
trg: Nkolo-masuwa asekaki lisusu.

src: "Then I'll teach you," he said.
trg: Alobaki, "Nakoteya yo."

src: Scene: Two friends, Jasmine and Joseph, are sitting at a coffee shop.
trg: Likambo: Baninga mibale, Jasmine na Joseph, bafandi esika batekaka kafe.

src: Jasmine: I'm so glad you could meet me today, Joseph.
trg: Jasmine: Nasepeli makasi ndenge okutani na nga lelo, Joseph.

src: I really need your help.
trg: Nazali mpenza na mposa ya lisungi na yo.

src: Joseph: Anything for you, Jasmine.
trg: Joseph: Nakoki kosala nyonso mpo na yo, Jasmine.

src: What's going on?
trg: Likambo yango ezali nini?

src: Jasmine: I'm having a really tough time at work.
trg: Jasmine: Nazali kokutana na mikakatano na mosala.

src: I'm not sure if I'm going to be able to keep my job.
trg: Nayebi te soki nakoka kobatela mosala na nga.

src: Joseph: Oh no, Jasmine.
trg: Joseph: Oh te, Jasmine.

src: I'm so sorry to hear that.
trg: Esali nga mpasi na koyoka yango.

src: Jasmine: It's a long story.
trg: Jasmine: Ezali lisolo ya molai.

src: But basically, my boss is really unfair to me.
trg: Kasi na mokuse, patron na nga azali kosalela nga makambo malamu te.

src: She's always picking on me and making me do all the worst jobs.
trg: Azali ntango nyonso kopona nga mpe kosalisa nga misala nyonso ya mabe.

src: And she's not even giving me a fair chance.
trg: Mpe azali kopesa nga kutu te libaku ya malamu.

src: Joseph: That's terrible, Jasmine.
trg: Joseph: Ezali mpasi, Jasmine.

src: I can't believe she's treating you like that.
trg: Nazali kondima te ete azali kosalela yo makambo ndenge wana.

src: Jasmine: I know.
trg: Jasmine: Nayebi.

src: I'm so stressed out about it.
trg: Nazali komitungisa mingi mpo na yango.

src: I don't know what to do.
trg: Nayebi te nasala nini.

src: Joseph: Well, first of all, you need to take a deep breath and calm down.
trg: Joseph: Malamu, ya liboso, osengeli kopema makasi mpe kokitisa motema.

src: The smell of fresh-baked bread wafted through the air as the baker pulled a tray of golden brown loaves from the oven.
trg: Nsolo ya mampa oyo bauti kotumba ezalaki koleka na mopepe ntango mosali-mampa abimisaki kikalungu ya mampa ya brun na furu.

src: He carefully set them on a cooling rack and smiled, pleased with his work.
trg: Atyaki yango na likebi na esika ya kokomisa yango malili mpe asekaki, azalaki na kosepela na mosala na ye.

src: The loaves were perfectly browned and had a delicious aroma that made his mouth water.
trg: Mampa ekomaki mpenza brun mpe ezalaki na nsolo ya kitoko oyo etondisaki nsoi na monoko na ye.

src: He couldn't wait to try one!
trg: Azalaki na mposa ya makasi ya komeka moko!

src: The baker cut a slice of bread and took a bite.
trg: Mosali-mampa akati eteni ya limpa mpe ameki.

src: It was even better than he had imagined, with a soft, chewy texture and a rich, flavorful taste.
trg: Ezalaki kutu elengi koleka ndenge nazalaki kokanisa, na langi ya pete mpe makasi mpe elengi ya makasi mpenza.

src: He closed his eyes and savored the moment, enjoying the feeling of contentment that came from eating something so delicious.
trg: Akangaki miso mpe asepelaki na ngonga wana, asepelaki na mayoki ya esengo oyo eutaka na kolya eloko ya kitoko makasi.

src: The baker knew that he was lucky to have the ability to bake such delicious bread.
trg: Mosali-mampa ayebaki ete azalaki na libaku ya malamu ya kozala na mayele ya kosala mampa wana ya kitoko makasi.

src: He took pride in his work and was always happy to share his creations with others.
trg: Azalaki kosepela na mosala na ye mpe azalaki na esengo ya kokabola mayele na ye na bato mosusu.

src: The type of fish you choose will depend on your personal preferences and the intended use for the fish.
trg: Lolenge ya mbisi okopona ekotalela mposa na yo moko mpe ndenge ozali kokana kosalela mbisi yango.

src: If you are looking for a fish that is high in omega-3 fatty acids, then you may want to choose a wild river fish.
trg: Soki ezali koluka mbisi oyo ezali na mafuta ya acide omega-3, na nsima okoki kopona mbisi mokolo ya ebale ya zamba.

src: These fish are typically lower in contaminants than farm-raised fish.
trg: Mbala mingi bambisi wana ezalaka na pwazo moke koleka bambisi babokolaka na ferme.

src: However, wild river fish can be more expensive and difficult to find.
trg: Kasi, mbisi ya ebale ya zamba ekoki kozala ntalo mingi mpe mpasi na kozwa.

src: If you are looking for a fish that is mild in flavor and easy to cook, then you may want to choose a calm lake fish.
trg: Soki ozali koluka mbisi oyo ezali elengi ya katikati mpe pete na kolamba, wana okoki kopona mbisi ya lac ya kimya.

src: These fish are typically not as high in omega-3 fatty acids as wild river fish, but they are still a good source of protein and other nutrients.
trg: Mbisi oyo ezalaka mpenza te na mafuta ya acide omega-3 ebele neti mbisi ya ebale ya zamba, kasi ezalaka esika ya malamu ya kozwa proteine mpe bavitamine mosusu.

src: Calm lake fish are also typically more affordable and easier to find than wild river fish.
trg: Mbisi ya lac ya kimya ezalaka mbala mingi na ntalo malamu mpe pete na kozwa koleka mbisi ya ebale ya zamba.

src: If you are looking for a fish that is low in cost and easy to care for, then you may want to choose a stock pond farm raised variety.
trg: Soki ozali koluka mbisi ya ntalo moke mpe ya pete na kobatela, wana okoki kolinga kopona mbisi moko oyo babokolaka na maziba ya ferme.

src: These fish are typically raised in controlled environments and are fed a diet that is designed to promote growth.
trg: Babokolaka mbisi oyo mbala mingi na bisika oyo balandelaka yango mpe batyaka yango na bilei oyo basalaka mpo na kolendisa bokoli.

src: Stock pond farm raised fish are typically not as high in omega-3 fatty acids as wild river or calm lake fish, but they are still a good source of protein and other nutrients.
trg: Bambisi babokolaka na maziba na ferme ezalaka mbala mingi te na mafuta ya acide omega-3 neti mbisi ya ebale ya zamba to ya lac ya kimya, kasi ezalaka kaka esika ya malamu ya kozwa proteine mpe bavitamine mosusu.

src: Ultimately, the best type of fish for you will depend on your individual needs and preferences.
trg: Na nsuka, lolenge ya malamu ya mbisi mpo na yo ekotalela bamposa na yo mpe makambo olingi.

src: Do some research to learn more about the different types of fish available and choose the one that is right for you.
trg: Sala mwa bolukiluki mpo na koyeba balolenge ekeseni ya bambisi oyo ezali mpe pona oyo ebongi mpo na yo.

src: Unsolved mysteries have captured the public's imagination for centuries.
trg: Mabombami eyebana te ebenda makanisi ya bato banda mibu ebele.

src: From the disappearance of Amelia Earhart to the identity of Jack the Ripper, these cases have left us wondering what really happened.
trg: Banda na kolimwa ya Amelia Earhart kino na koyeba Jack Ripper, makambo epusaka biso na komituna nini mpenza esalemaki.

src: While some of these mysteries may never be solved, they continue to fascinate us because they offer a glimpse into the unknown.
trg: Ata ndambo ya mabombami oyo ekotikalaka koyebana te, ezokokoba kosepelisa biso mpo esalisaka biso na koyeba mwa moke oyo eyebani te.

src: One of the most famous unsolved mysteries is the disappearance of Amelia Earhart.
trg: Moko ya mabombami ya ntina mingi mpenza oyo eyebana te ezali kolimwa ya Amelia Earhart.

src: Earhart was an American aviator who became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.
trg: Earhart azali mokumbi-mpepo ya Amerika oyo akomaki mwasi ya liboso ya kopumbwa ye moko mpo na kokatisa Mbu ya Atlantique.

src: In 1937, she set out on an around-the-world flight with navigator Fred Noonan.
trg: Na 1937, akendaki kotambola na mokili mobimba na mokumbi-masuwa Fred Noonan.

src: The pair disappeared over the Pacific Ocean on July 2, 1937, and their fate remains unknown.
trg: Bango mibale babungaki na Mbu ya Pacifique na mokolo ya 2 sanza ya Nsambo 1937, mpe makambo ekomela bango etikala koyebana te.

src: There are many theories about what happened to Earhart and Noonan.
trg: Ezali na mateya ebele etali makambo ekomelaki Earhart na Noonan.

src: Some believe that they crashed into the ocean, while others believe that they were captured by the Japanese.
trg: Bato mosusu bakanisaka ete mpepo epanzanaki na mbu, kasi basusu bakanisaka ete bato ya Japon bakangaki bango.

src: Still others believe that they deliberately disappeared in order to escape the public eye.
trg: Kasi bato mosusu bakanisaka ete balimwaka na nko mpo bato bamona bango te.

src: The mystery of Earhart's disappearance has been the subject of books, articles, and documentaries.
trg: Libombami ya kolimwa ya Earhart ekoma moto ya likambo ya mikanda, masolo, mpe badokimantere.

src: In 2017, a team of researchers announced that they had found evidence that Earhart's plane crashed on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean.
trg: Na 2017, etuluku moko ya balukiluki balobaki ete bamoni bilembeteli ya mpepo ya Earhart oyo epanzanaki na esanga ya mosika na Mbu ya Pacifique.

src: Giant wolf spiders are the largest species of arachnid in the world, with some individuals reaching lengths of over 12 inches.
trg: Balipungupungu ya minene ya mbwa ya zamba ezali bikelamu ya minene koleka na mokili, mpe misusu kati na yango ekomaka na molai ya koleka 12 inches.

src: They are found in tropical rainforests around the world, and are known for their aggressive behavior and venomous bite.
trg: Ezalaka na bazamba ya tropicale ya malili na mokili mobimba, mpe eyebana mpo na mobulu na yango mpe ngenge na yango ya monene.

src: Despite their fearsome reputation, giant wolf spiders are actually quite docile creatures.
trg: Ata ebangisaka, balipungupungu ya minene ya mbwa ya zamba ezalaka bikelamu ya botosi.

src: They are not aggressive towards humans unless they are provoked, and their venom is not typically fatal to humans.
trg: Bazalaka te mobulu epai ya bato longola kaka soki batumoli ye, mpe ngenge na bango ebomaka mpenza te bato.

src: However, their bite can be quite painful, and can cause swelling, redness, and itching.
trg: Kasi, ngenge na bango ekoki kozala mpasi, mpe ekoki kovimbisa, kokomisa mposo motano, to kosala mokusa.

src: Giant wolf spiders are excellent climbers, and can use their silk to create webs that can reach up to 30 feet in length.
trg: Balipungupungu ya minene ya mbwa ya zamba bayebi malamu komata banzete, mpe bakoki kosalela soie na bango mpo na kosala monyama oyo ekoki kokoma molai kino na 30 feet.

src: They are also very fast runners, and can move at speeds of up to 10 miles per hour.
trg: Bazali mpe bapoti-makasi ya mbango, mpe bakoki kotambola na vitesi ya 10 miles na ngonga.

src: Due to their size, speed, and climbing ability, giant wolf spiders are a popular choice for people who want to experience the thrill of riding a giant arachnid.
trg: Mpo na monene, vitese, mpe makoki na bango ya komata, balipungupungu ya mbwa ya zamba ezali liponi ya bato ebele oyo balingaka koyoka esengo ya komata na mpunda ya arachnide ya monene.

src: However, it is important to remember that these creatures are wild animals, and should be treated with respect.
trg: Kasi, ezali ntina kobosana te ete bikelamu oyo ezali banyama ya zamba, mpe esengeli kosalela yango makambo na botosi.

src: If you are thinking about riding a giant wolf spider, it is important to do your research and make sure that you are properly prepared.
trg: Soki ozali kokanisa komata na lipungungu monene ya mbwa ya zamba, ezali ntina kosala bolukiluki mpe kosala nyonso omibongisa malamu.

src: You should also make sure that you have the proper equipment, such as a harness and a leash.
trg: Osengeli kosala nyonso na kozala na bisaleli ebongi, neti nsinga ya kokanga mpo okwea te mpe nsinga ya kokamba ye.

src: Once you are properly prepared, you can begin your journey by finding a suitable giant wolf spider.
trg: Soki omibongisi malamu, okoki kobanda mobembo na yo na kozwaka lipungupungu monene ya mbwa ya zamba oyo ebongi.

src: Once you have found a spider, you can approach it slowly and gently.
trg: Soki ozwi lipungupungu ebongi, okoki kokende pene na yango na malembe mpe na boboto.

src: Once the spider is comfortable with you, you can slowly climb onto its back.
trg: Soki osepeli na lipungupungu, okoki komata na mokongo na yango na malembe.

src: Once you are on the spider's back, you can hold on tightly and enjoy the ride.
trg: Soki omati na mokongo na yango, okoki kosimba yango makasi mpe kosepela na kotambola.

src: The spider will use its silk to create a web that will support you as you ride.
trg: Lipungupungu akosalela soie na yango mpo na kosala monyama oyo ekosunga yo ntango ozali kotambola.

src: Riding a giant wolf spider is an unforgettable experience.
trg: Kotambola na lipungupungu ya mbwa ya zamba ya monene ezali likambo okotikala kobosana te.

src: It is a great way to experience the thrill of the wild, and to get up close and personal with one of the world's most fascinating creatures.
trg: Ezali lolenge ya malamu ya kokutana na esengo ya zamba, mpe kopusana pene mpenza na moko ya bikelamu ya koleka kitoko na mokili.

src: Fatima Messaoudi: I'm an actor and a furniture designer. I'm also passionate about flowers, especially those that bloom in the winter.
trg: Fatima Messaoudi: Nazali actrice mpe mokeli biloko. Nalingaka mpe mingi bafololo, mingimingi oyo ebimaka na eleko ya malili.

src: Interviewer: What drew you to acting and furniture design?
trg: Motuni-mituna: Nini epusaki yo na kokoma actrice mpe mokeli biloko?

src: Fatima Messaoudi: I've always loved performing and creating things.
trg: Fatima Messaoudi: Nalingaka ntango nyonso kozala actrice mpe kokela biloko.

src: Acting allows me to express myself creatively, and furniture design allows me to use my creativity to make something beautiful and functional.
trg: Kozala actrice esalisaka nga na komonisa mayele na nga ya kokela, mpe kokela biloko esalisaka nga na kosalela mayele wana mpo na kosala eloko ya kitoko mpe oyo ezali kosala.

src: Interviewer: What are some of the challenges you've faced as an actor and a furniture designer?
trg: Motuni-mituna: Mikakatano nini okutana na yango lokola actrice mpe mokeli biloko?

src: Fatima Messaoudi: One of the challenges I've faced as an actor is the lack of diversity in the industry.
trg: Fatima Messaoudi: Moko ya mikakatano nakutana na yango lokola actrice ezali kozanga bokeseni na mosala oyo.

src: I've often been told that I'm not the right type for a role because of my race or ethnicity.
trg: Bayebisa nga mbala mingi ete nabongi te mpo na mokumba moko mpo na mposo ya nzoto to ekolo na nga.

src: As a furniture designer, I've faced the challenge of breaking into a male-dominated industry.
trg: Lokola mokeli biloko, nakutana na mokakatano ya kosala esika mibale basalaka.

src: Interviewer: How have you overcome these challenges?
trg: Motuni-mituna: Ndenge nini olonga mikakatano wana?

src: Fatima Messaoudi: I've overcome these challenges by working hard and never giving up.
trg: Fatima Messaoudi: Nalonga mikakatano wana na kosalaka makasi mpe kolemba ata moke te.

src: Translation has many benefits, including increasing the relative value of content, improving accessibility, and opening up new markets.
trg: Libongoli ezali na matomba ebele, ata mpe komatisa motuya ya konteni, kosala ete bato ebele bamona yango, mpe kofungola bazando ya sika.

src: When content is translated, it becomes accessible to a wider audience, which can lead to increased sales and profits.
trg: Soki babongoli konteni, bato ebele mpenza bazalaka na makoki ya kotanga yango, ekoki komatisa koteka mpe benefisi.

src: In addition, translation can help to build relationships with customers in other countries and cultures.
trg: Lisusu, libongoli ekoki kosalisa na kosala boyokani na bakiliya na mikili mpe baculture mosusu.

src: By displaying content in multiple languages, businesses can show that they are committed to reaching a global audience.
trg: Soki batye makambo na nkota ebele, bato ya mombongo akoki kolakisa ete bamipesi na kosalela bato ya mokili mobimba.

src: This can help to build trust and credibility with potential customers.
trg: Ekoki kopusa bakiliya mosusu na kotyela bango motema mpe kondimela bango.

src: Here are some specific examples of how translation has benefited businesses: * A small business that sells handmade jewelry translated its website into Spanish, French, and German.
trg: Tala mwa bandakisa ya sikisiki ezali komonisa ndenge libongoli ememela mimbongo matomba: * Mombongo moko ya moke oyo ezalaki koteka mayaka basala na maboko ebongolaki site internet na yango na Espagnole, na Français mpe na Allemand.

src: As a result, it saw a significant increase in sales from international customers * A large corporation that manufactures medical devices translated its product manuals into multiple languages.
trg: Yango wana, bakomaki koteka biloko ebele na bakiliya ya mikili mingi * Kompani moko ya monene oyo esalaka ba aparei ya kimonganga ebongolaki mikanda ya biloko na yango na nkota ebele.

src: This helped to ensure that doctors and nurses in other countries could use the devices safely and effectively * A nonprofit organization that provides humanitarian aid translated its brochures and websites into dozens of languages.
trg: Esalisaka mpo minganga na ba infirmier ya bamboka mosusu basalela ba aparei wana malamu mpe na ndenge ebongi * Lisanga moko oyo elukaka matomba te oyo esungaka babola ebongolaki mikanda mpe basite internet na yango na nkota ebele.

src: This helped to reach people in need who would not have otherwise been able to access the organization's resources.
trg: Esalisaki na kobenda bato oyo bazali na mposa oyo bakokaki te kozwa biloko ya lisanga oyo na ndenge mosusu.

src: Translation is a powerful tool that can help businesses to grow and succeed.
trg: Libongoli ezali esaleli makasi oyo esalisaka mimbongo na kokola mpe na kolonga.

src: This is because we are all created in God's image, and God is the essence of rationality and order.
trg: Ezali mpo biso nyonso bakela biso na elili ya Nzambe, mpe Nzambe asalaka makambo mayoki te kasi na molongo.

src: When we live in accordance with our true nature, we are able to experience peace and harmony.
trg: Soki tozali na bomoi na kolanda bomoto na biso ya solo, tokoki kozwa kimya mpe boyokani.

src: However, when we allow our thoughts and actions to become chaotic and inconsistent, we experience inner conflict and turmoil.
trg: Kasi, soki totiki ete makanisi mpe misala na biso ekoma ya mabe mpe oyo elongobani te, tokozala na matata mpe mobulu na kati.

src: There are many ways to achieve internal consistency.
trg: Ezali na balolenge ebele ya kosala makambo ndenge moko na kati.

src: One way is to live according to our values.
trg: Lolenge moko ezali ya kotosa bizaleli na biso ya malamu.

src: When we know what is important to us and we make choices that are consistent with those values, we feel a sense of purpose and direction.
trg: Soki toyebi makambo nini ezali ntina mpo na biso mpe tozwi bikateli oyo ezali koyokana na bizaleli na biso, tokomona ee tokokisa mokano mpe tozwi litambwisi.

src: Another way to achieve internal consistency is to be honest with ourselves about our strengths and weaknesses.
trg: Lolenge mosusu ya kozala na boyokani na kati ezali ya kozala solo na biso moko na oyo etali makambo na biso ya malamu mpe ya mabe.

src: When we are aware of our true selves, we can make choices that are in alignment with our authentic nature.
trg: Soki toyebi malamu ndenge tozali mpenza, tokoki kozwa bikateli oyo eyokani na bomoi na biso ya solo.

src: Of course, achieving internal consistency is not always easy.
trg: Ya solo, kozala na boyokani ya kati ezalaka te ntango nyonso pete.

src: There will be times when we make mistakes or when we are faced with difficult choices.
trg: Ekozala na bantango oyo tokosala mabunga to tokokutana na maponi ya mpasi.

src: However, if we are willing to strive for consistency, we will eventually find our way back to peace and harmony.
trg: Kasi, soki tondimi kosala makambo kaka ndenge moko, nsukansuka tokozwa ndenge ya kozongela kimya mpe boyokani.

src: Vimes was having a headache.
trg: Vame azalaki koyoka moto mpasi.

src: It was the kind of headache that made you want to tear your hair out, or at least write a strongly worded letter to the makers of whatever it was that had given you the headache in the first place.
trg: Ezalaki lolenge ya moto mpasi oyo ekopusa yo olingi kolongola nsuki na yo, to kokoma mokanda ya nkanda mpenza na bato nyonso oyo basalaki likambo nyonso oyo esalaki ete oyoka moto mpasi na ebandeli.

src: In this case, the headache was the result of a particularly trying day at work.
trg: Na ndakisa oyo, moto mpasi eutaki na mokolo ya makasi na mosala.

src: Vimes had been investigating a series of robberies, and he was starting to feel like he was getting nowhere.
trg: Vimes azalaki kolandela miyibi ebele, mpe azalaki kobanda komiyoka neti azali kokende esika moko te.

src: He was tired, he was frustrated, and he just wanted to go home and sleep for a week.
trg: Alembaki, alembaki nzoto, mpe azalaki kolinga kaka kozonga ndako mpe kolala mposo mobimba.

src: As he was walking back to his office, Vimes passed a small stationery shop.
trg: Ntango azalaki kozonga na biro, Vimes alekaki liboso ya butiki moko ya bapapie.

src: In the window, he saw a sign that said "Best Letters in the City".
trg: Na fenetre, amonaki elembo bakomi ete "Mikanda ya Malamu Koleka na Engumba."

src: Vimes stopped and stared at the sign for a moment.
trg: Vimes atelemaki mpe azalaki kotala elembo wana mwa ntango.

src: He thought about his headache, and he thought about all the letters he had to write.
trg: Akanisaki moto mpasi na ye, mpe akanisaki mikanda nyonso oyo akomaki.

src: He sighed and went into the shop.
trg: Apemaki makasi mpe akendaki na butiki.

src: The shop was full of all sorts of stationery supplies.
trg: Butiki etondaki na bapaie ya lolenge nyonso.

src: There were pens, pencils, paper, envelopes, stamps, and even a few typewriters.
trg: Ezalaki na babiki, bacrayon, baamvelope, batimbre, mpe kutu mwa bamashine ya kokoma.

src: It is true that there exist in this world situations that defy all explanation, events so strange and wondrous that they seem to be the stuff of dreams or nightmares.
trg: Ezali solo ete ezali na makambo mosusu na mokili oyo likoki ya kolimbola yango ezali te, makambo ya kokamwa mpenza yango wana ekoki komonana neti ezali bandoto to bandoto ya mabe.

src: Such is the case with the story I am about to tell you, a tale of supernatural forces and the strange events that unfolded when they were unleashed upon the world.
trg: Ezali ndenge moko na lisolo nalingi kobetela biso, lisolo ya banguya oyo eleki ya bato mpe makambo ya kokamwa oyo esalemaki ntango babimaki na mokili.

src: It all began one night, when a group of friends were gathered together for a party.
trg: Nyonso ebandaki na butu moko, ntango etuluku moko ya baninga bazalaki kosangana mpo na feti.

src: They were drinking and laughing, enjoying each other's company, when suddenly the lights went out.
trg: Bazalaki komela mpe koseka, kosepela na boninga na bango, ntango na mbala moko bamwinda ekufaki.

src: The room was plunged into darkness, and the only sound was the sound of their own breathing.
trg: Ndako etondaki na molili, mpe makelele moko mpamba oyo ezalaki, ezalaki ya kopema na bango moko.

src: Then, in the darkness, they saw it: a strange, glowing light.
trg: Na nsima, na kati ya molili, bamonaki yango: pole ya kokamwa ezali kongenga.

src: It seemed to be coming from nowhere, and it was growing brighter and brighter.
trg: Emonanaki neti ezali kouta na esika te, mpe ezalaki kokoba kokoma monene.

src: The friends were terrified, but they were also curious.
trg: Baninga babangaki makasi, kasi bazalaki koluka mpe koyeba.

src: They wanted to know what this light was, and where it was coming from.
trg: Bazalaki kolinga koyeba soki pole wana ezalaki nini mpe ezalaki kouta na wapi.

src: Slowly, they approached the light.
trg: Malembemalembe, bapusaki na pole wana.

src: As they got closer, they could see that it was coming from a small, glowing sphere.
trg: Ntango bakomaki pene, bamonaki ete ezalaki kouta na esika ya moke, ya kongenga.

src: The sphere was hovering in the air, and it was surrounded by a faint aura.
trg: Eloko wana etikalaki esika moko na mopepe, mpe ezingamaki na mayoki ya kolemba.

src: "Dude, I'm so heartbroken right now. My girlfriend of 2 years just broke up with me."
trg: "Moninga, nazali na motema mpasi sikoyo. Sheri na nga oyo tosali bambula 2 auti koboya nga."

src: "What happened?"
trg: "Nini esalemaki?"

src: "I don't know. She just said she wasn't feeling it anymore.
trg: "Nayei te. Alobaki kaka azali kosepela na yango lisusu te.

src: I'm so confused.
trg: Nabulungani mpenza.

src: I thought we were happy."
trg: Nazalaki kokanisa azalaki na esengo."

src: "I'm sorry, man.I know how you feel. Heartbreak sucks."
trg: "Mawa mpenza, moninga. Nayebi ndenge ozali komiyoka. Motema mpasi ezala mpasi mingi."

src: "It does. I don't know what to do."
trg: "Ezali bongo. Nayebi te nasala nini."

src: "Just give yourself some time.
trg: "Mipesa kaka mwa ntango.

src: Cry it out if you need to.
trg: Lela soki likoki ezali.

src: And then, when you're ready, start to move on.
trg: Mpe na nsima, soki obongami, banda kokende liboso.

src: There are plenty of other fish in the sea."
trg: Ezali na bambisi mosusu ebele na mbu."

src: "I know. But I don't know if I'm ready to date again yet."
trg: "Nayebi. Kasi nayebi soki nazali ya kobongama na kolinga lisusu."

src: "That's okay. You don't have to be ready right away. Just take your time and heal."
trg: "Ezali malamu. Esengeli te kozala ya kobongama kaka sikoyo. Zwa ntango na yo mpe bika."

src: "Thanks, man. I appreciate it."
trg: "Matondi, moninga. Nasepeli."

src: "No problem."
trg: "Likambo te."

src: I have been living with type 1 diabetes for over 20 years.
trg: Nabela maladi ya diabte 1 banda bambula koleka 20.

src: I was diagnosed when I was just 10 years old, and it has been a lifelong journey.
trg: Bakangaki yango ntango nazalaki kaka na mibu 10, mpe ezali mobembo ya bomoi mobimba.

src: There have been many challenges along the way, but I have also learned a lot about myself and what it means to be a strong, resilient person.
trg: Nakutana na mikakatano ebele na nzela, kasi nayekola mpe makambo ebele mpo na nga moko mpe ndimbola ya kozala moto ya mpiko mpe akangaka motema.

src: One of the biggest challenges I have faced is managing my blood sugar levels.
trg: Moko ya mikakatano ya mpasi oyo nakutana na yango ezali kolandela nivo ya sukali oyo ezali na makila na nga.

src: Diabetes is a condition that affects the way your body turns food into energy.
trg: Diabete ezali maladi oyo ebebisaka lolenge nzoto na yo ekomisaka bilei energie.

src: When you eat, your body breaks down the carbohydrates in your food into glucose, which is then absorbed into your bloodstream.
trg: Soki olye, nzoto na yo ekomisaka ba carbohydrate oyo ezali na bilei na yo glucose, oyo na nsima ekotaka na kati ya makila.

src: Your pancreas releases insulin, a hormone that helps glucose get from your blood into your cells.
trg: Pancrea na yo ebimisaka insuline, oyo ezali hormone moko oyo esalisaka glucose euta na makila na yo mpo ekota na baselilena yo.

src: In people with type 1 diabetes, the pancreas doesn't make enough insulin, or it doesn't make any at all.
trg: Na bato oyo babelaka diabete 1, pancrea esalaka te insuline ya kokoka, to esalaka yango ata moke te.

src: This means that people with type 1 diabetes have to take insulin injections to help their bodies use glucose for energy.
trg: Elakisi ete bato oyo babelaka diabete ya lolenge 1 bazwaka bantonga ya insuline mpo na kosalisa nzoto na bango esalela glucose mpo na kozwa energie.

src: Managing my blood sugar levels can be a tricky business.
trg: Kolandela nivo ya sukali ezali na makila nga ekoki kozala mosala ya mpasi.

src: There are a lot of factors that can affect my blood sugar, including what I eat, how much I exercise, and how much stress I am under.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo ekoki kozala na bopusi na sukali kati na makila, ata mpe biloko nalyaka, mingi ya ngalasisi nasalaka, mpe basusi oyo nazali na yango.

src: I have to constantly monitor my blood sugar levels and make adjustments to my insulin doses as needed.
trg: Nasengeli kolandela ntango nyonso nivo ya sukali na makila na nga mpe kosala mbongwana na insuline na nga soki ezali ntina.

src: I was fortunate to attend a school that offered a wide range of AP courses and extracurricular activities, which gave me the opportunity to explore my interests and learn about different career paths.
trg: Nazalaki na libaku malamu ya kokota eteyelo oyo ezalaki na mateya ya AP mpe misala mosusu, yango epesa nga mabaku ya komona biloko nalingaka mpe koyekola misala ya ndenge na ndenge.

src: One of the most important things I learned in high school was how to think critically and solve problems.
trg: Moko ya makambo ya ntina nayekolaki na college ezalaki ndenge ya kokanisa ya ndenge ya mabe mpe kobongisa makambo.

src: My AP English and math classes taught me how to analyze text and data, and my science classes taught me how to design and conduct experiments.
trg: Bakelasi na nga AP ya Anglais mpe ya matematike eteyaki nga ndenge ya kolandela maloba mpe badonnée, mpe kelasi na nga ya siansi eteyaki nga ndenge ya kosala midele mpe komeka yango.

src: These skills have been essential in my college courses and my career as a software engineer.
trg: Mayele oyo ezalaki ntina mingi na mateya ta iniversite mpe na mosala na nga lokola enzeniere ya ba logiciel.

src: Another important thing I learned in high school was how to work effectively with others.
trg: Likambo mosusu ya ntina oyo nayekolaki na college ezalaki ndenge ya kosala malamu na bato mosusu.

src: My participation in extracurricular activities such as student government and the debate team taught me how to communicate my ideas clearly and persuasively, and how to work as part of a team to achieve a common goal.
trg: Bosangani na nga na misala mosusu neti koyekola guvernema mpe ekipi ya débat eteya nga ndenge ya kobimisa makanisi na nga na polele mpe na ndenge ya kondimisa, mpe ndenge ya kosala na etuluku mpo na kokokisa mokano kaka moko.

src: These skills have been invaluable in my career, where I often have to collaborate with others to solve complex problems.
trg: Mayele oyo esalisa nga mingi na mosala na nga, epai wapi esengaka mbala mingi nasala na bato mosusu mpo na kobongisa makambo ya mpasi.

src: Finally, my high school experience helped me to develop a strong work ethic and a commitment to excellence.
trg: Na nsuka, makambo nayekola na college esalisa nga na kozala na bizaleli ya malamu ya mosala mpe komipesa na kosala mosala malamu.

src: The challenging academic courses I took taught me the importance of hard work and perseverance, and the extracurricular activities I participated in taught me the value of teamwork and dedication.
trg: Mateya ya mpasi ya iniversite oyo nazwaki eteyaki nga ntina ya kosala makasi mpe ya kolendendela, mpe misala mosusu oyo nazwa eteya ngai ntina ya kosala mosala elongo mpe ya komipesa.

src: These qualities have helped me to succeed in college and in my career.
trg: Bizaleli oyo esalisa nga na kolonga na iniversite mpe na mosala na nga.

src: I am grateful for the opportunity to have attended a high school that provided me with such a strong educational foundation.
trg: Nazali na botondi mpo na libaku nazwaki ya kokota college oyo epesaki nga fondation oyo ya makasi ya mateya.

src: I believe that the skills and knowledge I gained in high school have helped me to become a successful college student and a professional.
trg: Nakanisi mayele mpe boyebi nazwaki na college esalisa nga na kokoma mwana ya kelasi mpe moto ya mosala oyo alonga.

src: Rainstorms are a common occurrence in many parts of the world, and they can have a significant impact on our lives.
trg: Mbula ya makasi ebetaka mingi na bisika mingi na mokili, mpe ekoki kozala na bopusi ya makasi na bomoi ya bato.

src: They can bring much-needed water to parched land, but they can also cause flooding, mudslides, and other damage.
trg: Ekoki komema mai na bisika oyo ekauka, kasi ekoki mpe komema mpela, bapotopoto, mpe makama mosusu.

src: Rainstorms are caused by the rising of warm air, which causes water vapor to condense and form clouds.
trg: Mbula ya makasi eutaka na komataka ya mopepe ya moto, oyo esalaka ete mopepe ya mai ekakangama mpe esala mapata.

src: When the water droplets in the clouds become too heavy, they fall as rain.
trg: Soki matanga ya mai oyo ezali na mapata ekomi kilo mingi, ekweaka lokola mbula.

src: The amount of rain that falls in a rainstorm is measured in inches.
trg: Bamekaka mingi ya mbula oyo ekweaka na mbula makasi na inches.

src: A light rainstorm might produce only a few inches of rain, while a heavy rainstorm can produce over a foot of rain.
trg: Mbula mwa makasi ekoki kokweisa kaka ba inches moko ya mbula, kasi mbula ya makasi mpenza ekoki kobimisa koleka foot moko ya mbula.

src: Rainstorms can have a variety of effects on our lives.
trg: Mbula ya makasi ekoki kozala na bopusi ekeseni na bomoi na biso.

src: They can wash away dirt and debris, making roads and sidewalks impassable.
trg: Ekoki komema mbindo mpe bosoto, mpe kosala ete likolo ya koleka na babalabala mpe banzela ezala te.

src: They can also cause power outages and flooding.
trg: Ekoki kosala ete lotiliki ekatana mpe komema mpela.

src: Flooding can be especially dangerous, as it can quickly sweep away people and property.
trg: Mpela ekoki kozala likama makasi, mpo ememaka noki bato na biloko.

src: Despite the potential dangers, rainstorms can also be beneficial.
trg: Atako ezali na makama, mbula ya makasi ekoki kozala na matomba.

src: They can help to improve soil quality and water the plants.
trg: Ekoki kosalisa na kokomisa mabele kitoko mpe kosopela banzete mai.

src: Rainstorms can also be a source of entertainment, as people enjoy watching the rain and listening to the thunder.
trg: Mbula ya makasi ekoki mpe lisano ya kitoko, mpo bato basepelaka kotala mbula mpe koyoka bankake.

src: Eyes are complex organs that allow us to see.
trg: Miso ezali binama ya mindondo oyo esalisaka biso na komona.

src: They are located in the front of the head and are protected by the eyelids.
trg: Ezalaka liboso ya moto mpe ebatelami na masala ya miso.

src: Each eye is made up of three layers: the sclera, the choroid, and the retina.
trg: Liso mokomoko esalemi na ba couche misato: sclera, choroide, mpe retine.

src: The sclera is the white part of the eye, the choroid is the dark layer behind the sclera, and the retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.
trg: Sclera ezali eteni ya mpembe ya liso, choroide ezali couche ya moindo nsima ya sclera, mpe retine ezali couche eyebaka pole, ezalaka nsima ya liso.

src: The retina contains millions of light-sensitive cells called rods and cones.
trg: Retine ezalaka na bamilio ya basilile oyo eyebaka pole, babengaka yango batonnet mpe cones.

src: Rods are responsible for night vision, while cones are responsible for color vision.
trg: Batonnet ekipaka pole ya butu, kasi cones ekipaka couleur ya pole.

src: When light hits the retina, it is converted into electrical signals that are sent to the brain via the optic nerve.
trg: Soki pole ekomi na retine, ebongolaka yango na bilembo ya lotiliki oyo etindamaka na boongo na nzela ya misisa ya miso.

src: My family has always kept animals.
trg: Libota na nga ebatelaka banyama ntango nyonso.

src: When I was a child, we had a dog, a cat, and a few fish.
trg: Ntango nazalaki mwana, tozalaki na mbwa, niawu, mpe mwa bambisi.

src: As I got older, we added a few more animals to the mix, including a rabbit, a guinea pig, and a hamster.
trg: Ntango nazalaki kokola, tobakisaki mwa bambisi mosusu mpo na etuluku wana, neti lapin, couchon d'Inde, mpe hamster.

src: I loved taking care of all of our animals and learning about their different needs.
trg: Nazalaki kolinga kobatela banyama na biso nyonso mpe koyekola bamposa na bango ekeseni.

src: One of my favorite animals that we ever kept was a rabbit named Cocoa.
trg: Moko ya banyama nazalaki kolinga mingi oyo tozalaki kobatela ezalaki lapin babengi Cocoa.

src: Cocoa was a brown and white Holland Lop rabbit.
trg: Cocoa azalaki lappin ya brun mpe mpembe ya Hollande Lop.

src: She was the sweetest animal I've ever met and she loved to be cuddled.
trg: Ezalaki nyama ya kitoko koleka oyo natikala kokutana na ye mpe azalaki kolinga babondela ye.

src: She was also very smart and could learn tricks like sit, stay, and come.
trg: Ezalaki mpe mayele mpe ekoki koyekola makambo neti kofanda, kotikala, mpe koya.

src: One day, I was playing with Cocoa in the backyard when I noticed that she was chewing on something.
trg: Mokolo moko, nazalaki kosakana na Cocoa na nsima y ndako mpe namonaki ezalaki kotafuna eloko moko.

src: I went over to investigate and saw that she was chewing on a piece of fiber from one of our clothes.
trg: Napusanaki mpo na koyeba mpe namonaki ezali kotafuna nsinga euti na moko ya bilamba na biso.

src: I took the fiber away from her and showed it to my mom.
trg: Nakamataki nsinga wana epai na ye mpe nalakisaki yango na mama.

src: My mom explained that rabbits need to eat fiber in order to digest their food properly.
trg: Mama alobaki ete balappin basengeli kolya nsinga to fibre mpo na ko digerer bilei na bango malamu.

src: She said that we should give Cocoa some hay to eat, which is a good source of fiber.
trg: Alobaki ete tosengeli kopesa Cocoa mwa matiti mpo na kolya, oyo ezali fibre ya malamu.

src: I gave Cocoa some hay and she loved it!
trg: Nabesaki Cocoa mwa matiti mpe asepelaki na yango!

src: You have no idea how the real world works, and you think that everything should be handed to you on a silver platter.
trg: Oyebi ata moke te ndenge mokili ya solo esalaka, mpe okanisi ete basengeli kopesa yo biloko nyonso na sani ya palata.

src: You're always complaining about something, and you never seem to be happy with anything.
trg: Ozali ntango nyonso komilelalela mpo na eloko moko, mpe emonani ete osepelaka na eloko moko te.

src: You're a bunch of entitled brats, and I'm sick of it.
trg: Bozali kaka etuluku ya bazoba, mpe nalembi yango.

src: Grow up.
trg: Bokola.

src: The world doesn't owe you anything.
trg: Mokili ezali na eloko ya kopesa bino te.

src: You have to work hard to get what you want.
trg: Bosengeli kosala makasi mpo na kozwa oyo bolingi.

src: There's no such thing as a free lunch.
trg: Bilei ya midi ya ofele ezala te.

src: If you want something, you have to go out and earn it.
trg: Soki olingi eloko moko, osengeli kobima mpe koluka yango.

src: Stop whining and complaining.
trg: Tika kolelalela mpe komilelalela.

src: It's not going to get you anywhere.
trg: Ekomeka yo esika moko te.

src: If you have a problem, then solve it.
trg: Soki ozali na likambo, silisa yango.

src: Don't just sit around and cry about it.
trg: Kosuka kaka te na kofanda mpe kolela mpo na yango.

src: Be more mature.
trg: Zala mokolo.

src: Act your age.
trg: Sala na kotalela mbula na yo.

src: You're not children anymore.
trg: Ozali lisusu te mwana ya moke.

src: It's time to start acting like adults.
trg: Ezali ntango ya kobanda komitambwisa lokola mikolo.

src: I'm tired of dealing with your childish behavior.
trg: Nalengi kobunda na bizaleli na yo ya kimwana ya moke.

src: If you don't start acting like adults, then I'm going to have to cut you out of my life.
trg: Soki obandi te kosala lokola mikolo, wana ekosenga nalongola yo na bomoi na nga.

src: I don't have time for your nonsense.
trg: Nazali na ntango mpo na makambo ezangi ntina.

src: Grow up and start acting like adults, or I'm out of here.
trg: Kola mpe banda kosala makambo neti mikolo, soki te nakolongwa awa.

src: I was recently cleaning out my attic when I came across a box of old recipes that had been passed down from my grandmother.
trg: Kala mingi te nazalaki kokombola likolo ya ndako mpe namonaki kesi oyo ezali na biloko ya kala oyo koko na nga ya mwasi apesaki nga.

src: Some of them were quite old, dating back to the early 1900s.
trg: Mosusu ezali ya mwa kala, ezali ya ebandeli ya mibu 1900.

src: I was curious to see what they were, so I started reading through them.
trg: Nazalaki kolinga koyeba soki ezali nini, yango wana nabandaki kotanga yango.

src: One recipe in particular caught my eye.
trg: Lolenge moko ya kolamba bilei esepelisaka nga.

src: It was for an anti-aging facial mask made with honey, yogurt, and oatmeal.
trg: Ezalaki masque ya kobundisa kokoma mobange esalemi na mafuta ya nzoi, yayourt, mpe farine ya avoka.

src: I decided to give it a try, and I was amazed at the results!
trg: Nazwaki ekateli ya komeka yango, mpe mbano na yango ekamwisaki nga!

src: My skin looked so much smoother and younger after using it.
trg: Mposo na nga ezalaki komonana pete mingi mpe elenge nsima ya kosalela yango.

src: I'm so glad I found this old recipe.
trg: Nazali na esengo mpo namonaki eloko wana ya kala.

src: It's a real treasure, and I'm sure it will remain in my family for many years to come.
trg: Ezali libula ya solo, mpe nandimi ete etikala na libota na biso na bambula mingi ezali koya.

src: The veteran sat alone in the hospital room, staring at the blank television.
trg: Soda ya kala afandaki ye moko ya chambre ya lopitalo, azali kotala televizio ya mpamba.

src: He had been in the hospital for weeks, and he was starting to go stir-crazy.
trg: Asali bamposa mingi na lopitalo, mpe abandaka kozwa nkanda.

src: He had been in a lot of wars, and he had seen a lot of death and destruction.
trg: Akenda na bitumba ebele, mpe amona liwa ya bato ebele mpe biloko ebele oyo babebisa.

src: But nothing had ever prepared him for this.
trg: Kasi eloko moko te ebongisa ye mpo na likambo oyo.

src: The door to his room opened, and a young woman walked in.
trg: Porte ya chambre na ye efungwamaki, mpe elenge moko ya mwasi akotaki.

src: She was carrying a bouquet of flowers. "Hello," she said. "My name is Sarah.
trg: Azalaki komema liboko ya bafololo, "Mbote," wana maloba na ye. "Nkombo na nga Sarah.

src: I'm a volunteer here at the hospital."
trg: Nazali mosali ya bolingo malamu awa na lopitalo."

src: The veteran smiled. "It's nice to meet you, Sarah," he said.
trg: Mobange asekaki. "Esengo na kokutana na yo, Sarah," wana maloba na ye.

src: "What are you doing here?"
trg: "Ozali kosala nini awa?"

src: "I'm here to make you laugh," she said. "Laughter is the best medicine, you know."
trg: "Nayei awa mpo na kosekisa yo," wana maloba na ye. "Koseka ezali nkisi ya malamu, ndenge oyebi."

src: The veteran laughed. "I'm not sure I can laugh," he said.
trg: Soda ya kala asekaki. "Nandimi te ete nakoki koseka," wana maloba na ye.

src: "I've been through a lot."
trg: "Nakutanaka na makambo ebele."

src: "I know," Sarah said. "But I'm going to make you laugh."
trg: "Nayebi," wana maloba ya Sarah. "Kasi nakosekisa yo."

src: And she did.
trg: Mpe asalaki yango.

src: She told jokes and stories, and she even did some magic tricks.
trg: Abetelaki ye maseki mpe masolo, mpe asalaki kutu mwa makambo ya kokamwa.

src: The veteran laughed until his sides hurt.
trg: Soda ya kala asekaki kino munoko esalaki ye mpasi.

src: A typical day for a person in Nigeria might start with a cup of tea or coffee and a breakfast of bread, eggs, and plantains.
trg: Mokolo ya bato mingi ya Nigeria ekoki kobanda na kopo ya thé to ya kafe mpe bilei ya ntondo ezali na mampa, maki, mpe lituma.

src: The workday typically starts around 8am and ends around 5pm, with a lunch break in the middle of the day.
trg: Mokolo ya mosala ebandaka pene ya 8am mpe esukaka pene ya 5pm, mpe kopema mpo na kolya ya midi ezalaka na katikati ya mokolo.

src: After work, people might relax at home with their families, go out to dinner, or attend a cultural event.
trg: Nsima ya mosala, bato bakoki kominyolisa na ndako na mabota na bango, kokende kolya libanda, to kokende na molulu ya culture.

src: The evening is often spent socializing with friends and family.
trg: Mbala mingi na mpokwa bazalaka na baninga mpe libota.

src: The daily routine of a Nigerian can vary depending on their location and lifestyle.
trg: Makambo moto ya Nigeria asalaka mokolo na mokolo ekoki kobongwana na kotalela esika azali mpe bomoi na ye.

src: In rural areas, people may wake up earlier to tend to their farms or livestock.
trg: Na bamboka, bato bakoki kolamuka na ntongo makasi mpo na kokipe baferme to bibwele na bango.

src: In urban areas, people may have more time for leisure activities.
trg: Na bingumba, bato bakoki kozala na ntango ebele mpo na masano.

src: However, some aspects of daily life are common across Nigeria, such as the importance of family and community.
trg: Kasi, makambo mosusu ya bomoi ya mokolo na mokolo ezalaka na bisika nyonso na Nigeria, neti ntina ya libota mpe lisanga.

src: Nigeria is a diverse country with a rich culture, and the daily lives of its people reflect this diversity.
trg: Nigeria ezali mboka ya bonkoko ekeseni, mpe bomoi ya mokolo na mokolo ya bato na yango emonisaka bokeseni wana.

src: From the bustling cities of Lagos and Abuja to the more rural areas of the country, there is no one-size-fits-all description of what a typical day in Nigeria is like.
trg: Banda na bingumba ya mobulungano neti Lagos mpe Abuja kino na bisika ya bamboka, ezali te na ndimbola kaka moko mpo na kolobela ndenge bomoi ya mokolo na mokolo ezalaka na Nigeria.

src: But one thing is for sure: no matter where you are in Nigeria, you will find people who are warm, welcoming, and eager to share their culture with you.
trg: Kasi likambo moko ezali solo: ata ozali esika nini na Nigeria, okokuta bato oyo motomoto, ya boyambi, mpe oyo bazali na mposa ya kokabola culture na bango na yo.

src: The Nyasaland African Congress (NAC) was founded in 1944 by Dr. Hastings Kamuzu Banda and other Malawian nationalists.
trg: Lisanga Nyasaland ya Afrika (NAC) esalemaki na 1944 na Monganga Hastings Kamuzu Banda mpe balingi-mboka mosusu ya Malawi.

src: The NAC was the first political party in Malawi to advocate for African independence from British colonial rule.
trg: NAC ezalaki parti politiki ya liboso na Malawi oyo ezalaki kosenga lipanda ya Afrika na maboko ya bokonzi ya nkanza ya Grande-Bretagne.

src: In 1953, the NAC was banned by the British colonial authorities, but it continued to operate underground.
trg: Na 1953, NAC epekisamaki na bakonzi ya nkanza ya Grande-Bretagne kasi ekobaki kosala na nsense.

src: In 1961, the NAC was legalized and renamed the Malawi Congress Party (MCP).
trg: Na 1961, NAC endimamaki na mibeko mpe ekomaki na nkombo Parti ya Congres ya Malawi (MCP).

src: The MCP won the first general elections held in Malawi in 1964, and Dr. Banda became the first Prime Minister of Malawi.
trg: MCP elongaki maponi ya liboso ya bato nyonso oyo esalemaki na malawi na 1964, mpe Monganga Banda akomaki Ministre ya Yambo ya Malawi.

src: In 1966, Malawi became a republic, with Dr. Banda as the first President.
trg: Na 1966, Malawi ekomaki repiblike, mpe Monganga Banda azallaki Prezida ya liboso.

src: Dr. Banda ruled Malawi as a one-party state for 30 years.
trg: Monganga Banda ayangelaki Malawi na parti moko mpamba ya leta mibu 30.

src: He was a controversial figure, but he is also credited with modernizing Malawi and bringing it independence.
trg: Azalaki moto ya matata, kasi balobaka mpe ete ye moto akomisa Malawi ya sika mpe amemela yango lipanda.

src: The physicians, who are members of the Southern Medical Association, say that the firm's building was not properly ventilated and that the employees were exposed to harmful chemicals.
trg: Minganga, oyo bazalaki bato ya Lisanga ya Minganga ya Sude, balobi ete bandako ya kompani ezalaki te na mopepe ya malamu mpe ete bato ya mosala bazalaki kotika bango bazala na biloko mabe ya chimie.

src: "We were concerned about the health of the employees at this firm," said Dr. Raymond Neal-Kennedy, a spokesman for the SMA.
trg: "Tozalaki komitungisa mpo na kolongono ya nzoto ya bato ya mosala ya kompani wana," wana maloba ya Monganga Raymond Neal-Kennedy, molobeli ya SMA.

src: "The building was not up to code and the employees were being exposed to dangerous chemicals. We had no choice but to shut the firm down."
trg: "Ndako eyokanaki te na bakode mpe batikaki bato ya mosala bakutana na biloko ya mabe ya chimie. Tozalaki te na likambo ya kosala longola kokanga kompani wana."

src: The architecture firm, which has not been named, has denied the allegations.
trg: Architekte ya kompani, oyo nkombo na yango eyebani te, aboyaki makambo bafundaki ye.

src: The firm's owner, Mr. Ishq Kasawa, says that the building was properly ventilated and that the employees were not exposed to any harmful chemicals.
trg: Nkolo kompani, Monsieur Ishq Kasawa, alobi ete ndako ezali na mopepe ya malamu mpe ete bato ya mosala bazalaki te kokutana na biloko ya mabe ya chimie.

src: "We are disappointed by the actions of the SMA," said Mr. Kasawa.
trg: "Makambo SMA ezali kosala elembisi biso nzoto," wana maloba ya Monsieur Kaswa.

src: "We believe that we have been unfairly targeted. Our building is safe and our employees are healthy."
trg: "Tokanisi ete balandeli biso kozanga ntina. Ndako na biso ezali malamu mpe bato ya mosala bazali nzoto kolongono."

src: The SMA says that it will continue to investigate the matter and that it will take further action if necessary.
trg: SMA alobi ete ekokoba kolandela likambo oyo mpe ete ekosala makambo mosusu soki ezali ntina.

src: The Libyan Civil War is an ongoing armed conflict in Libya that began in 2011 with the overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi's government.
trg: Bitumba ya Bana-Mboka ya Libye ezali bitumba oyo esilkaka te na Libye; ebandaki na 2011 ma kokwea ya boyangeli ya Mummar Gaddafi.

src: After the fall of Tripoli, the Libyan National Transitional Council (NTC) proclaimed the establishment of the Libyan Interim Government, but the country descended into a state of lawlessness with two rival governments, the NTC and the Libyan National Army (LNA), and a number of militias vying for power.
trg: Nsima ya kokwea ya Tripoli, Lisanga ya Transition ya Ekolo Libye (NTC) balobaki batye Boyangeli ya Ntango Moke ya Libye, kasi mboka ekomaki na etat ya kobuka mibeko oyo ezali na biyangeli mibale, NTC mpe Basoda ya Ekolo Libye (LNA), mpe basoda ebele oyo bazali koluka kozwa bokonzi.

src: In 2014, the Libyan House of Representatives (HoR) was elected in the eastern city of Tobruk, but the HoR has been unable to exercise effective control over the country.
trg: Na 2014, bavotaki Lisanga ya Mimonisi ya Libye (HoR) na engumba Tobruk oyo ezali na este, kasi HoR ezali kokoka te koyangela mboka ndenge ebongi.

src: In 2016, the Government of National Accord (GNA) was formed in Tripoli under the auspices of the United Nations, but the GNA has been unable to gain control of the country's eastern regions.
trg: Na 2016, basalaki Boyangeli ya Boyokani ya Ekolo (GNA) na Tripoli na nse ya bokambi ya Nations-Unies, kasi GNA ekoka te koyangela bituka ya este ya ekolo oyo.

src: The LNA, led by Khalifa Haftar, has been fighting against the GNA and its allies in the west of the country.
trg: LNA, ekambami na Khalifa Haftar, ezali kobundisa GNA mpe baninga na yango na weste ya ekolo.

src: The conflict has led to a humanitarian crisis, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced from their homes.
trg: Bitumba oyo emema crise humanutaire, ebongo bankoto ya bato bakima bandako na bango.

src: The United Nations has called for an immediate ceasefire and the start of a political dialogue.
trg: Nations-Unies esenga bakata bitumba kozanga kozela mpe babanda masolo ya politiki.

src: As the twentieth century drew to a close, computers and electronics were becoming increasingly intertwined.
trg: Ntango ekeke ya ntuku mibale ekomaki na nsuka, ba ordinatere mpe biloko ya elektronike ebandaki kosangana mingi mpenza.

src: In the early days of computing, these two fields were largely separate.
trg: Na mikolo ya ebandeli ya ordinatere, biloko mibale oyo ezalaki mpenza ya kokabwana.

src: Computers were large, expensive machines that were used for scientific and military purposes.
trg: Ba ordinatere ezalaki bamashine ya minene mpe ya ntalo mingi oyo bazalaki kosala mpo na makambo ya siansi mpe ya basoda.

src: Electronics were used in a variety of consumer products, such as radios, televisions, and telephones.
trg: Bazalaki kosalela biloko ya elektronike na biloko ekeseni, neti baradio, batelevizio, mpe batelefone.

src: However, as computers became smaller and more affordable, they began to be used in a wider variety of applications.
trg: Kasi, ntango ba ordinatere ebandaki kokoma mike mpe kitoko mingi, babandaki kosalela yango na ba application ebele.

src: This led to a blurring of the lines between computers and electronics.
trg: Esalaki ete ekoma mpais na koyebana bokeseni kati ya ba ordinatere mpe biloko ya elektronike.

src: One of the most significant developments in the history of computers and electronics was the invention of the personal computer (PC).
trg: Moko ya bokoli ya ntina na lisolo ya ba ordinatere mpe ya biloko ya elektronike ezalaki bosali ya ordinatere ya moto (PC).

src: The PC was first introduced in the 1970s, and it quickly became a popular tool for both personal and business use.
trg: Babimisaki PC na mbala ya liboso na mibu 1970, mpe eumelaki na kokoma esaleli ya ntina mpo na moto ye moko mpe mombongo.

src: PCs were originally designed for use in homes and offices, but they soon found their way into other settings, such as schools and libraries.
trg: Na ebandeli, basalaki ba PC mpo basalela yango na bandako mpe babiro, kasi ekotaki mpe na bisika mosusu, neti biteyelo mpe babiblioteke.

src: The PC's portability and versatility made it an ideal tool for a wide range of tasks, from word processing to gaming.
trg: Ndenge bakoki komema PC na pete mpe ekoki kosala makambo ebele esala ete ezala esaleli mpo na misala ebele, banda na kosala mosala kino na masano.

src: The development of the PC also led to the development of a new industry: the software industry.
trg: Bosali ya PC emema mpe na bokoli ya mosala ya sika: mosala ya ba logiciel.

src: Software companies created programs that could run on PCs, and these programs quickly became essential tools for PC users.
trg: Bakompani ya ba logiciel esalaki baprograme oyo ekoki kosala na ba PC mpe baprograme oyo ekomaki noki bisaleli ya ntina mpo na basaleli ya PC.

src: The hajj is a once-in-a-lifetime pilgrimage to Mecca, Saudi Arabia, that is required of all Muslims who are physically and financially able to make the journey.
trg: Hajj ezali mobembo basalaka mbala moko na bomoi mobimba mpo na kokende na Mecque, na Arabie Saoudite, oyo basengaka Bamizilma nyonso oyo na makoki ya mosuni mpe ya mbongo mpo na kosala mobembo wana.

src: The pilgrimage is one of the five pillars of Islam, and it is considered to be the most important spiritual journey a Muslim can make.
trg: Mobembo ya losambo ezali moko ya makonzi mitano ya losambo ya Mizilma, mpe bamonaka yango lokola mobembo ya ntina mingi ya elimo oyo Mizilma akoki kosala.

src: The hajj takes place over five days in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah.
trg: Hajj esalemaka na boumeli ya mikolo mitano na sanza ya Dhu al-Hijjah ya Bamizilma.

src: During the hajj, pilgrims perform a series of rituals that commemorate the life of Prophet Muhammad and the prophets who came before him.
trg: Na ntango ya hajj, bato basali mobembo ya losambo basalaka milulu ebele oyo ekundwelaka bango bomoi ya Mosakoli Muhammad mpe basakoli oyo bazalaki liboso na ye.

src: These rituals include walking around the Kaaba, the sacred black stone that is the center of the Great Mosque in Mecca; drinking from the Zamzam Well, which is believed to have healing powers; and standing on Mount Arafat, where Prophet Muhammad gave his final sermon.
trg: Milulu wana ezali kotambola zingazinga ya Kaaba, libanga ya moindo ya mosantu oyo ezali na katikati ya Mosque Monene na Mecque; komela na Libulu Zamzam, oyo bakanisaka ezali na nguya ya kobikisa; mpe kotelema na Ngomba Arafat, esika Mosakoli Muhammad asalaki lisukulu na ye ya nsuka.

src: The hajj is a physically and emotionally demanding journey, but it is also a time for Muslims to come together in worship and to reflect on their lives.
trg: Hajj ezali mobembo ya mpasi na nzoto mpe na mayoki, kasi ezali mpe ntango oyo Bamizlma bakutanaka elongo mpo na kosambela mpe kokanisa bomoi na bango.

src: It is a chance to renew their faith and to reaffirm their commitment to Islam.
trg: Ezali libaku ya kokomisa kondima na bango ya sika mpe ya kondimisa komipesa na bango na losambo ya Mizilma.

src: For many Muslims, the hajj is a life-changing experience.
trg: Mpo na Bamizilma mingi, hajj ezali likambo oyo ebongolaka bomoi.

src: It is a time to leave behind the stresses of everyday life and to focus on their spiritual journey.
trg: Ezali ntango ya kobosana basusi ya bomoi ya mokolo na mokolo mpe ya kotya likebi na mobembo ya elimo.

src: The rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns are making it more difficult to grow crops in some areas, while at the same time creating new opportunities for agriculture in other areas.
trg: Komata ya molunge mpe mbongwana ya ndenge mbula ebetaka ezali kosala ete ezala mpasi mingi na kokolisa milona na bisika mosusu, mpe kosala mabaku ya sika ya kosala bilanga na bisika mosusu.

src: The overall effect is that the global agricultural system is becoming more complex and less predictable.
trg: Bopusi mobimba ezali ete ebongiseli ya mosala ya bilanga ezali kokoma mpasi koleka mpe mpasi na koyeba.

src: One of the most direct effects of climate change on agriculture is the increase in the frequency and severity of extreme weather events.
trg: Moko ya bopusi ya mbala moko ya mbongwana ya climat na mosala ya bilanga ezali komata ya bambala mpe ya bokasi ya bacondition ya météo ya mabe mpenza.

src: Heat waves, droughts, floods, and storms can all damage crops and livestock, and make it difficult for farmers to get their crops to market.
trg: Mbonge ya moto, kokauka, bambula, mpe mipepe makasi, biloko oyo nyonso ekoki kobebisa milono mpe bibwele, mpe kosala ete ezala mpasi mpo basali-bilanga bazwi biloko ya koteka.

src: In some cases, these events can cause entire crop yields to be lost, leading to food shortages and price increases.
trg: Na bandakisa mosusu, makambo oyo ekoki kosala ete babungisa biloko nyonso oyo balongoli na bilanga, komema na kozanga bilei mpe na komata ntalo ya biloko.

src: In addition to extreme weather events, climate change is also leading to changes in the average temperature and precipitation patterns.
trg: Longola ba condition ya meteo ya mabe mpenza, mbongwana ya climat mpe ezali komema mpe mbongwana na molunge mpe na ndenge mbula ebetaka.

src: These changes are making it more difficult to grow some crops in certain areas, while at the same time creating new opportunities for agriculture in other areas.
trg: Mbongwana oyo ezali kosalela ete ezala mpasi mpo milona ekola na bisika mosusu, mpe ezali kobimisa mabaku ya sika mpo na mosala ya bilanga na bisika mosusu.

src: For example, the warmer temperatures in some areas are making it possible to grow crops that were previously not possible, while the increased precipitation in other areas is making it possible to grow crops that were previously not feasible.
trg: Na ndakisa, molunge ya makasi na bisika mosusu ezali kosalisa na kokolisa milona oyo kala bakokaki kokolisa te, mpe ndenge bambula ezali kobeta ebele na bisika mosusu ezali kosalisa na kokolisa milona oyo kala ezali mpasi na kokolisa.

src: I was driving home from work one day when I got cut off by another driver.
trg: Nazalaki kozonga na ndako na motuka mokolo moko nsima ya mosala ebongo motuka mosusu alekaki liboso na nga.

src: I was so angry that I started tailgating him and flashing my lights.
trg: Nasilikaki makasi yango wana nabandaki kolanda pene na nsima mpe kongengisa bamwinda na nga.

src: He just kept driving slower and slower, and I was getting more and more frustrated.
trg: Akobaki kokumba malembemalembe, mpe nazalaki kaka kolemba nzoto.

src: Finally, I couldn't take it anymore.
trg: Nsukansuka, nakokaki lisusu te kokanga motema.

src: I pulled up next to him and started yelling at him.
trg: Nakendaki na mopanzi na ye mpe nabandaki kogangela ye.

src: He rolled down his window and started yelling back at me.
trg: Akitaki vitre na ye mpe abandaki kogangela nga.

src: We were both so angry that we were shaking.
trg: Biso mibale tozali na nkanda yango wana tozalaki kolenga.

src: The other driver pulled over to the side of the road, and I followed him.
trg: Mokumbi wana mosusu akendaki kotelema mopanzi ya nzela, mpe nalandaki ye.

src: We got out of our cars and started yelling at each other even louder.
trg: Tobimaki na mituka mpe tobandaki kogangelana na mongongo makasi.

src: I was so close to hitting him that I could smell his breath.
trg: Nazalaki pene ya kobeta ye mpo nazalaki koyoka nsola ya kopema na ye.

src: Just when I thought it couldn't get any worse, a police car pulled up.
trg: Kaka ntango nakanisaki ete ekoyinda mpenza, motuka ya polisi eyaki.

src: The officer got out of his car and asked us what was going on.
trg: Polisi abimaki na motuka na ye mpe atunaki biso nini ezali koleka.

src: We both told him our sides of the story, and he started writing us a ticket.
trg: Biso mibale tobetelaki ye lisolo moto na moto na ndenge na ye, mpe abandaki kokomela biso tike.

src: As I was walking back to my car, I realized that I had learned my lesson.
trg: Ntango nazali kozonga esika motuka na nga ezali, namonaki ete nazwi liteya.

src: Road rage is never worth it.
trg: Nkanda ya nzela ezali na ntina te.

src: It's not worth getting angry over, and it's not worth getting a ticket.
trg: Ezali na ntina ya kosilika, mpe ezali na ntina te ya kozwa tike.

src: Once upon a time, there was a beautiful river that flowed through a lush forest.
trg: Na ntango moko boye, ezalaki na ebale moko ya kitoko ezalaki koleka na zamba ya kitoko.

src: The river was home to many creatures, including fish, frogs, turtles, and birds.
trg: Ebale wana ezalaki na bikelamu ebele, neti bambisi, magorodo, bankoba, mpe bandeke.

src: The river was also a popular spot for humans to swim, fish, and relax.
trg: Ebale ezalaki mpe esika oyo bato bazalaki kolinga kobeta mai, koloba, mpe kominanola.

src: One day, a young girl named Lily was playing near the river when she saw a turtle caught in a fishing net.
trg: Mokolo moko, elenge moko ya mwasi nkombo na ye Lily azalaki kosakana pene ya ebale mpe amonaki nkoba ekangami na monyama.

src: Lily knew that she had to help the turtle, so she ran home to get her father.
trg: Lily ayebaki ete asengeli kosalisa nkoba, yango wana akendaki noki kozwa papa na ye.

src: Lily's father helped her to free the turtle, and the two of them returned to the river.
trg: Papa ya Lily asalisaka ye na kolongola nkoba, mpe bango mibale bazongaki na ebale.

src: The turtle thanked Lily for saving her life, and Lily promised to always be kind to animals.
trg: Nkoba etondaki Lily mpo abikisaki ye, mpe Lily alakaki ete akozalaka ntango nyonso boboto na banyama.

src: Lily continued to visit the river often, and she always made sure to look out for any animals that might be in danger.
trg: Lily akobaki kokende kotala ebala mbala na mbala, mpe azalaki ntango nyonso koluka kotala soki ezali na nyama oyo azali na likama.

src: One day, Lily saw a group of boys throwing rocks at the fish in the river.
trg: Mokolo moko, Lily amonaki etuluku ya bilenge ya mibali bazali kobwaka mabanga na bambisi na mai.

src: Lily knew that she had to stop them, so she ran up to the boys and told them that what they were doing was wrong.
trg: Lily ayebaki ete asengeli kopekisa bango, yango wana akendaki epai ya bilenge wana mpe ayebisaki bango ete likambo bazalaki kosala ezalaki malamu te.

src: The boys were surprised to hear this from Lily, but they listened to her and stopped throwing rocks.
